2803f6386e37cdcd: NEW YORK: A US judge rejected on Wednesday a request by the Justice Department to temporarily block California from counting any mail ballots for the Nov 3 midterm elections received from people on a list of more than 20,000 registered voters the Trump administration alleges are likely noncitizens.

The decision marks the latest setback for President Donald Trump's effort to boost the federal government's role in elections ahead of the midterms, with his Republican Party locked in a tight battle to retain control of both houses of Congress.

US District Judge David Carter issued the decision after a hearing on Tuesday in Los Angeles federal court over the Justice Department's request for a temporary restraining order barring officials from counting any ballots from the individuals it flagged.
The Justice Department filed the lawsuit on Oct 15, a rare intervention in the voting process weeks before an election.

California has said the state's safeguards against noncitizen voting are robust. It said the Justice Department's assertions relied on "suspect data" and that complying with its demands would risk disenfranchising eligible voters.
California is the most populous US state and a Democratic stronghold. It has more seats in the House of Representatives — 52 — than any other state.

Trump has made California a focal point of his sweeping immigration crackdown since returning to the White House, accusing it of undermining public safety through its "sanctuary state" policies that ‌limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
Trump has repeatedly insisted that states are not doing enough to stop voting by noncitizens, which he says is widespread despite multiple studies and state audits showing it is rare.

The hearing comes after a federal appeals court on Monday rejected an unusual emergency request by the Justice Department asking the appeals court to temporarily block California from counting the ballots before Carter had the chance to rule.
The Justice Department did not indicate how many of the more than 20,000 people it flagged in California had actually submitted a mail ballot.
Apart from California, the Trump administration has sought to intervene in elections in two states that are home to competitive races, Alaska and Washington State.
25abde9968e91671: ROME. Oct 29 — Popemobiles past and present from German automaker Mercedes-Benz are the stars of a new show at the Vatican Museums, emblematic vehicles that serve to bring the pope closer to his flock.

“A Century of the Popemobile” tracks the long relationship between the Stuttgart-based automaker and the Holy See, where the head of the Catholic Church has used increasingly sophisticated vehicles to meet the faithful, whether in St Peter’s Square, or during papal voyages around the world.
Opening to the public today, the exhibit in a temporary pavilion within the Vatican’s Square Garden features eight models borrowed from the automaker’s collection and that of the Vatican.

First on display — and poles apart from the white popemobiles of present-day — is the Nurburg 460, a shiny black Pullman limo delivered to Pope Pius XI in 1930, whose luxurious exterior reveals a plush papal seat inside, covered in raspberry silk brocade.
Last is the hulking ML 500 made for Pope Benedict XVI in 2012, with its enlarged enclosed back section allowing for optimal viewing of, and by, the pope.

Sandro Barbagallo, head of the museum’s department of historical collections, told journalists during a preview yesterday that the popemobile should not be viewed as “just a simple means of transport”.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Visitors look at one of the historic papal vehicles on display at the Square Garden (Giardino Quadrato) during the press preview of the ‘A Century of Papamobile’ exhibition, in the Vatican Museums, in Vatican City October 28, 2026. — AFP pic

“The so‑called popemobile serves to allow people to see the pope, but also to allow him to see. It serves so that people can greet the pope, but also and above all so that the pope can, along the roads, greet and at the same time bless,” he said.
“It is a modern technology placed at the service of the pontiff, at the service of his ministry,” said Barbagallo.
The first so-called modern popemobile appeared in 1980, with the Mercedes-Benz 230G for Pope John Paul II.
Its rear resembled an elevated throne covered by a transparent dome, adorned with mother of pearl paintwork and gold trim.

Other cars on display include the 1960 300D Landaulet with its plush beige mohair seat and removable side windows for Pope John XXIII and the 1997 lungo Landaulet with its electrohydraulic soft top for Pope John Paul II.

Although the show recounts 100 years of papal mobility, it leaves out the various vehicles produced by Mercedes-Benz’s competitors and gifted to the pope, including from Fiat, Renault, Volkswagen — and even Ferrari.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The exhibition ‘A Century of the Popemobile’, which presents eight historic vehicles mapping 100 years of papal mobility, will open its doors on October 29, 2026. — AFP pic
‘Sardine can’
Popemobiles have included bulletproof glass since the assassination attempt on John Paul II in 1981 in Rome.
But for all their benefits, the popemobiles sometimes meet resistance from those they were designed to transport.

Pope Francis famously told a Spanish newspaper in 2014 that he couldn’t get close to the people from within his “sardine can” popemobile encased in bulletproof glass, saying he preferred to be more out in the open, despite the safety risks.
For short trips to cross Rome, Francis often opted for a simple white Fiat.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Historic papal cars, including models with luxurious upholstery and protective glass enclosures, are on display in a new exhibition celebrating the Vatican’s motoring heritage. — AFP pic

Accessing the show, visitors enter through the museum’s Carriage Pavilion with the ornate horse-drawn coaches of popes and cardinals of years past, before global automakers began wooing the pope with their vehicles.

Speaking to journalists, the chief executive of Mercedes-Benz Heritage, Marcus Breitschwendt, said the automaker’s historic cars, including popemobiles, are exhibited in a closely protected museum in Stuttgart.
“A clear rule to everybody” prevails there, Breitschwendt said.
“It’s strictly forbidden to everybody, even to our CEO, to all of us, to sit on the pope’s seat.
“And that’s the way it will stay.” — AFP
d5f0695e8773b008: WASGHINGTON, Oct 29 — US President Donald Trump demanded yesterday that Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola and a rival sharing the name of Alaska’s Republican incumbent be removed from next week’s election ballot, accusing Democrats of an illegal scheme to confuse voters.

His call followed a New York Times investigation reporting that Democratic operatives had secretly recruited so-called “spoiler” candidates, including another Dan Sullivan, in an effort to draw votes away from Republican Senator Dan Sullivan.
“It has just been determined that the Democrats in Alaska illegally searched for, and recruited, a man named Dan Sullivan,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

He accused Democrats of committing perjury by making false statements under oath in federal court, and demanded that the incumbent be allowed to run without either Peltola or the “FAKE Dan Sullivan” on the ballot.
And he told reporters later that Peltola and any other alleged accomplices should be prosecuted. “To me, that’s voter fraud at the highest level,” he said.
But the Times noted that recruiting candidates to split an opponent’s vote—a practice known as ballot stacking—is generally legal and has been used by both parties in Alaska.
As recently as 2024, little-known former Republican Anthony Frascone beat Democrat Mondaire Jones in a low-turnout Working Families Party primary in New York state.
Jones’s campaign and the leftist WFP accused Frascone of being a Republican spoiler. Local Democratic leaders and a group of voters sued to remove him, but a Westchester judge kept him on the ballot.
The Times investigation did not establish criminal wrongdoing in the Alaska case or substantiate Trump’s allegation of perjury.

The effort involved senior aides and lawyers for Peltola, as well as officials at the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC), according to the newspaper, which cited interviews, dozens of text messages and documents prepared for a potential lawsuit against the campaign.
Peltola ‘definitely aware’
Among those it said were recruited was Daniel J. Sullivan, a retired teacher from a remote Alaskan fishing community. He has said he entered the race of his own volition.
The newspaper identified Democratic operative Jerid Kurtz as a central figure, reporting that he traveled around Alaska under an assumed name to court potential candidates.
The Times said Kurtz also urged a Democrat to quit the race after the August primary, opening a place on the four-candidate ranked-choice ballot for Republican Gerald Heikes, also a recruit.
Heikes told the paper he was recruited by a Midwesterner who he did not think resembled a photo of Kurtz. Kurtz did not respond to requests for comment from the Times.
Peltola’s former campaign manager Elisa Rios told the paper the candidate was “definitely aware” of the project but not directly involved, and that DSCC aides had introduced Kurtz to the campaign.
Rios, who was fired in August and had been planning a wrongful termination lawsuit, later sought to retract her statements. The Times said her account was consistent with its other reporting.
Peltola’s campaign and the DSCC have denied recruiting any candidates.
The revelations come days after Trump ordered the Justice Department to sue Alaska over the presence of the second Sullivan on the ballot.
The lawsuit seeks to delay certification if Peltola narrowly defeats the incumbent and votes cast for his namesake could have changed the outcome.
In June Alaska’s Supreme Court upheld the retired teacher’s right to run, rejecting Republican efforts to remove him from the ballot.
The state has asked a federal judge to dismiss the Justice Department’s lawsuit, arguing it has no legal basis. — AFP
05fbd3b81be964a0: From Martin Vengadesan
I couldn’t help but be struck by the contrasting leadership styles on display in the run-up to the Melaka polls.
While neither is a candidate for chief minister, both PKR’s Adam Adli and Umno’s Dr Akmal Saleh are the faces of the future for their respective parties.
To me, Adam of PKR displays a soft-spoken, progressive style. There is backbone to his principles, and he was a student leader who was detained and harassed by the previous regime.
He chose to join a multiracial party and has progressed from PKR Youth chief to deputy minister of higher education after winning the Hang Tuah Jaya parliamentary seat.
While he often comes under the cosh over the failed PTPTN loan abolition, I have seen him at work trying to extend the benefits of our nation to its less fortunate.
On the other hand, there’s the rabble-rousing Akmal of Umno. The two men were born a year apart but represent very different ways of thinking.
Indeed, his career reads to me like a hall of shame. But presumably, it has some appeal among the rempit crowd.

Just last week came another defamation suit loss, as the Melaka High Court ruled in Teresa Kok’s favour over his September 2024 remarks slamming her for questioning a proposed mandatory halal certification.
Kok was awarded RM250,000 in general and aggravated damages, plus RM50,000 in costs. He had called her an “old Nyonya” and suggested placing a non-halal logo on her forehead.

Now he says he is prepared to give up his bid to defend the Merlimau state seat in the Melaka election on Nov 14 if the court case he faces over a charge under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code hurts Umno and Barisan Nasional’s chances at the polls.
Akmal is charged with making statements on his Facebook page that allegedly caused public fear, alarm, or disruption to public order.
The charge stems from a viral Facebook video and post made around Aug 11, 2025, regarding an incident in which the Jalur Gemilang was displayed upside down.
Akmal said he had conveyed his position to Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, stressing that the party’s interests must come before his personal ambitions.
This is, of course, merely the latest transgression by a man who has positioned himself as an ethnic champion. Akmal was also previously involved in a defamation suit brought by his sibling.

In 2024, he called on the prime minister to sack tourism, arts and culture minister Tiong King Sing after bak kut teh was recognised as a national heritage food. In the same year, he was involved in a dispute over vernacular schools that led to an insinuation that his opponent, P Ramasamy, was drunk.
And of course he led the KK Mart boycott campaign after socks bearing the word “Allah” were discovered on sale there. Is his brand of politics toxic or constructive? I leave you to decide.

Adam has been working quietly to build consensus. The fact that he cares about all Malaysians does not make him any less of a member of his race or religion. In fact, that is one of the great false assumptions in Malaysian public life.
In his roles at the higher education ministry and the youth and sports ministry, Adam has supported several public-facing initiatives, including PTPTN loan repayment flexibility.

Under the repayment measures announced in the 2027 budget, borrowers earning between RM2,501 and RM3,000 a month are required to make minimum monthly payments of RM50, while those earning below RM2,500 a month are eligible for repayment exemptions.

Other initiatives for students include support for transit passes like My50 and MyKomuter50, alongside the FlySiswa flight subsidy of RM500 for students who travel between Peninsular Malaysia and East Malaysia.
He has promoted technical and vocational education and training (TVET) to bolster graduate employability and supported the revival of the Rakan Muda programme for youth development.
He has also been involved in local infrastructure and welfare projects in Hang Tuah Jaya, such as local flood mitigation.
More than anything else, he views the future with a keen mind and open heart. These are the leaders we need if we are to stop going around in circles.
Martin Vengadesan is a former editor who currently serves as a strategic communications consultant to the communications ministry.

9dc1d0679d35761b: Saya tidak dapat mengelak daripada melihat perbezaan ketara antara gaya kepimpinan yang ditonjolkan menjelang PRN Melaka.
Walaupun kedua-duanya bukan calon ketua menteri, Adam Adli dari PKR dan Dr Akmal Saleh dari Umno boleh dianggap sebagai wajah generasi masa depan parti masing-masing.

Pada pandangan saya, Adam menampilkan pendekatan progresif dan bersahaja. Namun, beliau tetap teguh dengan prinsipnya. Adam pernah menjadi pemimpin mahasiswa yang ditahan dan berdepan tekanan ketika pemerintahan terdahulu.

Beliau kemudiannya memilih untuk menyertai sebuah parti berbilang kaum dan perjalanan politiknya berkembang daripada ketua Pemuda PKR kepada timbalan menteri pendidikan tinggi selepas memenangi kerusi Parlimen Hang Tuah Jaya.
Walaupun sering dikritik berhubung kegagalan memansuhkan pinjaman PTPTN, saya sendiri melihat usahanya untuk memastikan manfaat pembangunan negara turut dinikmati golongan kurang bernasib baik.
Berbeza pula dengan Akmal dari Umno yang lebih dikenali dengan pendekatan lantang dan konfrontasi. Kedua-duanya hanya berbeza usia setahun, tetapi mencerminkan cara berpolitik yang sangat berlainan.
Bagi saya, rekod politik Akmal dipenuhi kontroversi. Namun, pendekatan itu mungkin mempunyai tarikannya tersendiri dalam kalangan kelompok tertentu, termasuk golongan mat rempit.

Minggu lalu, beliau sekali lagi kalah dalam saman fitnah apabila Mahkamah Tinggi Melaka memutuskan memihak kepada Teresa Kok berhubung kenyataannya pada September 2024 yang mengecam Ahli Parlimen Seputeh itu kerana mempersoalkan cadangan mewajibkan pensijilan halal.
Kok dianugerahkan ganti rugi am berjumlah RM250,000, selain kos RM50,000. Akmal sebelum itu menggelarnya sebagai 'Nyonya tua' dan mencadangkan supaya logo tidak halal diletakkan pada dahinya.

Kini, Akmal berkata beliau bersedia melepaskan peluang mempertahankan kerusi DUN Merlimau pada PRN Melaka 14 Nov ini sekiranya kes mahkamah yang dihadapinya mengikut Seksyen 505(b) Kanun Keseksaan menjejaskan peluang Umno dan Barisan Nasional (BN).
Beliau didakwa membuat kenyataan menerusi Facebook yang didakwa boleh menimbulkan ketakutan atau kegentaran awam, atau mengganggu ketenteraman awam.
Pertuduhan itu berkaitan video dan hantaran Facebook yang tular sekitar 11 Ogos 2025 mengenai insiden Jalur Gemilang dipasang secara terbalik.
Akmal berkata beliau sudah menyampaikan pendiriannya kepada Presiden Umno Zahid Hamidi dan menegaskan bahawa kepentingan parti perlu didahulukan berbanding cita-cita peribadinya.

Namun, ini hanyalah kontroversi terbaharu membabitkan seorang ahli politik yang meletakkan dirinya sebagai pejuang kepentingan kaum. Sebelum ini, Akmal juga pernah berdepan saman fitnah yang dikemukakan oleh adik-beradiknya.

Pada 2024, beliau menggesa Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim memecat Menteri Pelancongan, Seni dan Budaya Tiong King Sing selepas bak kut teh diiktiraf sebagai makanan warisan negara. Pada tahun sama, pertikaian mengenai sekolah vernakular turut menyaksikan beliau membuat kenyataan yang memberi gambaran bahawa lawannya, P Ramasamy, berada dalam keadaan mabuk.
Dan tentunya, Akmal juga mengetuai kempen memboikot KK Mart selepas stoking tertera kalimah 'Allah' didapati dijual di rangkaian kedai serbaneka itu.
Sama ada pendekatan politik seperti ini membawa manfaat atau sebaliknya, saya serahkan kepada pembaca untuk menilainya.
Adam pula memilih untuk bekerja secara lebih senyap dalam membina muafakat. Keprihatinannya terhadap semua rakyat Malaysia tidak menjadikannya kurang Melayu atau kurang Islam.
Sebenarnya, tanggapan seperti itu merupakan antara kekeliruan besar yang masih wujud dalam kehidupan masyarakat Malaysia.

Sepanjang berkhidmat di Kementerian Pendidikan Tinggi serta Kementerian Belia dan Sukan, Adam menyokong beberapa inisiatif yang memberi manfaat secara langsung kepada orang ramai, termasuk langkah memberi kelonggaran dalam pembayaran balik pinjaman PTPTN.

Di bawah langkah pembayaran balik yang diumumkan dalam Belanjawan 2027, peminjam berpendapatan antara RM2,501 hingga RM3,000 sebulan diwajibkan membuat bayaran minimum RM50 sebulan, manakala mereka yang berpendapatan kurang RM2,500 sebulan layak mendapat pengecualian bayaran balik.

Antara inisiatif lain untuk pelajar ialah bantuan bagi pas perjalanan seperti My50 dan MyKomuter50, selain subsidi penerbangan FlySiswa sebanyak RM500 untuk pelajar yang berulang-alik antara Semenanjung dengan Sabah dan Sarawak.
Adam turut mempromosikan pendidikan dan latihan teknikal dan vokasional (TVET) bagi meningkatkan kebolehpasaran graduan serta menyokong penghidupan semula program Rakan Muda untuk pembangunan belia.
Beliau juga terlibat dalam projek infrastruktur dan kebajikan di Hang Tuah Jaya, termasuk usaha mitigasi banjir di kawasan berkenaan.
Lebih penting daripada semua itu, beliau melihat masa depan dengan fikiran yang terbuka dan keprihatinan terhadap orang lain.
Pemimpin dengan pendekatan sebegini diperlukan sekiranya kita mahu berhenti mengulangi permasalahan sama tanpa bergerak ke hadapan.
Martin Vengadesan ialah bekas editor yang kini berkhidmat sebagai perunding komunikasi strategik kepada Kementerian Komunikasi.
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
9deaed0c6db1e0a5: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Malaysian Information Department (Japen) has implemented the Info On Wheels (IOW) programme at 23,962 locations nationwide, reaching an audience of 1.65 million from January 1 to September 23, in an effort to expand the dissemination of information related to the Madani Government’s policies, assistance and initiatives.

The Communications Ministry said that 5,571 JIWA@Komuniti Madani: Sembang Santai programmes were also implemented during the same period, involving 616,961 members of the Madani Community to enhance public understanding of various government initiatives.

He said that the programme is among the government’s comprehensive, inclusive, and continuous communication strategies implemented through face-to-face approaches, narrative coordination, publication of communication materials and digital dissemination, taking into account the needs of different target groups.

“To ensure that the message conveyed is consistent and easily understood, 231 narratives and pointers related to policies, assistance, programmes, and achievements of the Madani Government have been prepared as a reference for field officers.

“The narrative encompasses four main frameworks, namely the economy for the people, leadership with integrity, national unity and consistent achievements, with an emphasis on explaining the benefits of policies to the people using easily understandable language,” the ministry stated in a written response on the Parliament portal today.

The ministry answered Suhaizan Kaiat’s (PH-Pulai) question regarding the government’s communication strategy in addressing the public’s confusion about government policies and benefits, which makes them easily influenced by false information and propaganda.

In expanding digital reach, the ministry reported that 9,294 posts were uploaded on Japen’s official social media, including 1,298 creative content pieces that recorded 16.51 million views as of September 22.

It said the effort was supported through the publication of 50 brochures, 35 bulletins and four booklets, in addition to organising 68 exhibitions that attracted 162,900 visitors and the use of 4,000 screens through strategic partners.

It also said that the government will continue to strengthen integrated communication through various channels to ensure that the people receive accurate, clear, and easily understandable information, thereby enabling them to make fact-based assessments and not be easily swayed by misleading narratives.

Meanwhile, in response to Datuk Siti Aminah Aching’s (BN-Beaufort) question regarding the level of high-speed internet coverage and the issue of weak or no internet access in that parliamentary area, the Ministry of Communications said that 37 areas were identified as experiencing problems with that facility from January 1 to September 1.

Following that, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) issued 104 Notices of Non-Compliance to service providers between March 11 and August 5 to obtain improvement plans at the affected locations.

“A total of 51 instances of non-compliance have been resolved through the optimisation of the existing network, while another 33 will be addressed via improvements to network coverage and capacity. The remaining 20 require further action through a Commission Directive,” the ministry stated.

The ministry also said that internet and communication coverage in the populated areas of the Beaufort parliamentary constituency has reached 99.57 per cent as of Sept 1 through the National Digital Network Plan (Jendela), with 29 communication towers completed, 113 transmitter stations upgraded, and 7,526 premises equipped with fibre optic access.

For the 5G network, Digital Nasional Berhad (DNB) provides coverage to 20 per cent of populated areas through one transmitter site, while U Mobile Sdn Bhd achieves 42.80 per cent coverage through five upgraded transmitter sites as of the same date. — Bernama
e60d3c86ed71aebb: UNITED NATIONS: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) chief Luke Lindberg said Wednesday that the hunger situation in the Gaza Strip is "unacceptable" as he pledged to defend his staff against attacks, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported.
Speaking at a news conference at UN headquarters in New York, Lindberg said that "there is a very serious need" in Gaza, citing funding cuts as a major constraint on the agency's work.
Asked how he would address Israeli troops firing on WFP convoys, given his White House connections, Lindberg said staff security is "the number one concern for me."
"I will absolutely stand up for our employees, no matter where on Earth they are located," he said.
He added that "if anywhere in the world there are people attacking humanitarians, I will absolutely do what I can to protect them from violence against them and their families."

Outlining his priorities, Lindberg said: "First and foremost, it is protecting and empowering our staff members. Humanitarians have been killed all over the world in the past two years, at unprecedented levels, and it's unacceptable."
"Over 700 people in the last few years have been killed trying to save other people's lives, and nobody should lose their life trying to save someone else's," he added.
Asked about the WFP's partnership with the US, which backed his candidacy, Lindberg said the "United States plays a critical role. It is the largest funder for the World Food Programme."
"When I was nominated for this role by the United States, president (Donald) Trump personally called me," he said. "I have a great relationship with many members of the Trump administration."
Lindberg stressed the need for broader donor support. "There is no one nation, no one entity that can do this alone. We have to do it together," he added.
ef0a3799c6086ba6: MIAMI, Oct 29 — Brazil’s defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro insisted yesterday he is his country’s rightful leader, after fleeing to the United States to start a self-imposed exile.
Bolsonaro’s defiance on arrival in Florida signaled continued upheaval for Brazil, where leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a dramatic runoff election Sunday.

“I am the elected president, and the criminals who stole Brazil’s election are part of a criminal organization that has established a tyranny,” Bolsonaro said in the statement published on his X account, slamming “electoral fraud.”
“I will lead the opposition from here,” he said. In a subsequent statement, he revised his claim, saying he is the “leader,” rather than “president.”
Bolsonaro, 45, touched down yesterday in a private jet at Opa-Locka Executive Airport near Miami.
Rogerio Marinho, the leader of Bolsonaro’s Liberal Party in the Senate, told reporters in Brasilia that he was in “solidarity” with the former candidate, describing him as a “political exile.”
However, he distanced himself from Bolsonaro’s statement, and refused to back up Bolsonaro’s claims of electoral fraud.
“The Liberal Party cannot make that claim,” he said. “There is no evidence of that.”
Flavio Bolsonaro “is an expression of the right in Brazil today...he calls himself a leader and it’s true: he’s a leader,” Marinho told reporters.

US President Donald Trump’s hard-right administration has strong links to Bolsonaro and his father Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest in Brazil after attempting to overturn his own electoral loss to Lula in 2022.
Trump reiterated his stand that Brazil’s election was “very strange” but told reporters he “won’t get involved” in Flavio Bolsonaro’s claim to the presidency.
Details of how Bolsonaro, accompanied by his wife and daughters, made it to US soil are still emerging.

He is under investigation in his home country over alleged corruption and money laundering. With his current parliamentary immunity about to expire, he was ordered to surrender his passports but left anyway, reaching the United States via Argentina and Ecuador.

A police source told AFP that Bolsonaro’s Brazilian and diplomatic passports had been canceled, but the senator has also held Italian nationality since 2023, according to Italian documents seen by AFP.
The US Department of Homeland Security said in a statement that the Bolsonaro family members were inspected and cleared “with applicable immigration laws and procedures.”
The travel ban was issued by powerful Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, who led the case against Bolsonaro’s father and is a controversial figure hated by the Brazilian right.
Shameful’ act
Lula, who won Sunday’s election with 51.8 per cent of the vote, called Bolsonaro’s departure a “shameful” act.
“A person who sneaks out of their country must have something to hide,” he said in Brasilia during his 81st birthday celebration on Tuesday.
But Brazil police issued a statement saying that he was not considered a fugitive.
There was controversy in neighboring Argentina, where opposition lawmakers demanded to know how Bolsonaro had managed to transit through the country.

While Argentinian authorities said he was carrying valid travel documents, officials have requested chief of cabinet Diego Santilli to provide details to parliament, according to opposition lawmaker Agustin Rossi.
Fraud cases
The most high-profile fraud case against Bolsonaro in Brazil centers on the unreleased biopic “Dark Horse” starring US actor Jim Caviezel as Flavio’s father Jair.

In May, the outlet Intercept Brasil revealed audio recordings in which Flavio Bolsonaro negotiated approximately $24 million to finance the film with banker Daniel Vorcaro, who is jailed over one of Brazil’s biggest-ever fraud cases.
Before the leak, Flavio Bolsonaro had denied knowing Vorcaro, or that he had financed the movie.
In July, the Supreme Court ordered a probe into the film’s financing, and whether it involved corruption, money laundering or the illegal movement of currency.
Bolsonaro acknowledged Vorcaro had funded the film, but insisted it was a private business deal that was “completely legal.” — AFP

a50b1a77fa067005: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — A meeting involving state executive councillors (Exco members) to discuss developments in the orange economy is expected to be held in the third week of November or by the end of the month, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the proposed working committee would involve state Exco members and ministers to discuss the progress of the orange economy in their respective states.
Fahmi said he had recently presented a note on the proposed establishment of the committee at the Meeting of Mentris Besar and Chief Ministers.

He said the discussions would focus on feedback and proposals from state governments, including identifying potential film locations, craft products, cultural groups and animation teams that could be promoted and supported.
“This is important because we need to obtain feedback, views, findings and proposals from Exco members and state ministers on the creative economy,” he said.

He was speaking to reporters after the Lembah Pantai Parliamentary Deepavali Aid Presentation Ceremony at IWK Eco Park@Pantai Dalam here last night, organised by the Lembah Pantai Member of Parliament’s Office in collaboration with Minnal FM.

Also present were Communications Ministry Deputy Secretary-General (Telecommunications Infrastructure) Mano Verabathran and Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) Editor-in-Chief Arul Rajoo Durar Raj.
Fahmi said the government needed time to obtain feedback from state governments before the Orange Economy Council met again.
“We need a little more time at that level. We expect the Orange Economy Council to meet again in the first quarter of next year,” he said.
The Orange Economy Council (MEJ) was established a few months ago and is chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, with membership comprising several ministries.
Earlier, Fahmi presented RM150 vouchers to about 600 families in the Lembah Pantai parliamentary constituency in conjunction with Deepavali to help ease their cost of living and festive preparations.

He said the vouchers could be redeemed at selected outlets, including Checkers Hypermarket, Mydin Mart Pantai Dalam, TMC Bangsar and Econsave Scott Garden in Jalan Klang Lama, from October 23 to November 18, 2026.

Fahmi said the government had also introduced various initiatives to assist the Indian community, including an allocation of RM150 million through the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (MITRA), as well as RM150 million each through Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia (AIM) and the National Entrepreneurial Group Economic Fund (Tekun).
He said cooperation with relevant agencies and Minnal FM would be undertaken to improve the Indian community’s understanding of and access to the various government assistance programmes available.

In Lembah Pantai, Fahmi said efforts were also being made to improve facilities at Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Tamil (SJKT) Bangsar and SJKT Saraswathy, both categorised as under-enrolled schools. These included purchasing new laptops for their computer laboratories and upgrading infrastructure.
“This is important to me. I want these two Tamil national-type schools to remain in Lembah Pantai. We will ensure that they can continue operating,” he said. — Bernama
9d390ff6ee7a69c1: TOKYO: An earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 5.5 struck the northeastern part of Chiba Prefecture, near Tokyo, early Thursday, Kyodo News reported, citing the country's weather agency.

The quake, which occurred at 12.07am local time and measured lower 5 on the Japanese seismic intensity scale, originated at a depth of about 52 kilometres and posed no tsunami threat, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.

A lower 5 reading was recorded in Yokoshibahikari, while weaker shaking was registered in other parts of the prefecture. The quake was also felt in Tokyo and neighbouring prefectures, including Tochigi, Ibaraki and Saitama.
The agency initially reported the quake's magnitude as 5.4 and estimated that it had occurred at a depth of about 50km.
40968bc76a46bf56: PETALING JAYA: Kepong MP Lim Lip Eng has called on Inspector-General of Police Khalid Ismail and Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar to disclose how many of the 2,097 police officers and personnel arrested from 2021 to August this year have been charged, convicted or dismissed from the force.

In a written parliamentary reply to Lim on Tuesday, home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail revealed that 1,551 of the police officers and personnel arrested from 2021 to August this year were nabbed for drug-related offences. Sixty-four were arrested in relation to robberies, and 482 were arrested by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission.

In a statement today, Lim said the 2,097 arrests amounted to an average of more than one police officer or personnel member being arrested daily over the five years and eight months, describing the figure as a "severe blow" to the integrity of the police force.
"The police are supposed to arrest criminals, not become criminals themselves. How can the public continue to trust the police if they are involved in crime?" said Lim, a lawyer by training.

"And these are just three categories of offences... They do not include the various other crimes not specified in the minister’s reply. What is the actual number of police officers and personnel arrested for all offences?"

Lim also questioned the delay in investigating a case involving 12 police officers suspected of robbing a group of Chinese nationals of cryptocurrency worth about RM200,000 in Country Heights, Kajang, on Feb 5.
The 12 police personnel, including four officers from the Bukit Aman commercial crime investigation department, were detained for suspected involvement in a gang robbery.
Khalid previously said the policemen had been assigned to desk duties to ensure that the investigation could proceed properly.
In his written parliamentary reply to Lim, Saifuddin said the case remained under investigation, more than eight months after the incident.
Lim contrasted this with the case of Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency chief Shuhaily Zain, who was charged in court 23 days after an incident at KLIA.
"The inspector-general of police and the attorney-general should explain the difference in the investigation timelines," he added.
Shuhaily was charged in the Sepang magistrates’ court on Oct 21 with assaulting two policemen last month.
19d8d1aff1be2c11: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today expressed deep grief over the tragic loss of lives in the train collision in Spain.
In a Facebook post, he said Malaysia stood in solidarity with the people of Spain at this difficult time.
"Our thoughts are with all those who have lost loved ones, and we wish the injured a swift recovery," he said.
Anwar also paid tribute to the emergency personnel and others working tirelessly at the scene.

"On behalf of the government and people of Malaysia, I extend our deepest condolences to Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, the government and people of Spain, and especially to the families of the victims," Prime Minister said.

Yesterday, media reports said the death toll from Wednesday's high-speed train collision in central Spain has more than doubled to at least 64 people, according to the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha, making it even deadlier than a devastating rail accident near Adamuz in January.
However, the Malaysian Embassy in Madrid has yet to receive confirmation of any Malaysians affected by the collision involving two high-speed passenger trains.
c1d8f9f4e1275d37: OSLO, Oct 29 — Norway’s tourism authority yesterday used President Donald Trump’s derogatory comments about the country to vaunt the beauty of its toilets.

The US president, highlighting his anger at not winning the Nobel Peace Prize, called Norway a “shithouse country” at a rally on Sunday. Trump added that he did not want migrants from the Nordic state.

“We heard some noise about the ‘s+++house country’. Well, what we can say, we do have some of the most spectacular toilets in the world. With Love, Visit Norway,” the tourism agency said in a Facebook post.
It added pictures of some of the elegant latrines that it boasts with the headline ‘Meet the world’s most beautiful (s++t h++++s) toilets.”
Pictured was one rest room at the bottom of a hill overlooking a fjord. Others were situated next to a river or with various breathtaking panoramas in the country renowned for its rugged countryside.
Trump let rip at a rally in Michigan ahead of the US mid-term elections next week.
“Frankly, Norway sucks. Norway has become a shithouse country, actually,” he declared.
Trump said he would welcome immigrants from certain countries but not Norway “because I didn’t get the Nobel Prize.”
This year’s peace prize, awarded by a Norwegian committee, went to South African judge and rights defender Navi Pillay.
In general, Trump’s comments had little impact in Norway. Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide responded by maintaining that the government has no role in the Nobel peace prize.
“He (Trump) knows very well that the Nobel Committee is independent. We have reminded him of that, in case anyone is wondering — and that is still the case,” he said. — AFP
250c541b6058a742: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Umno has confirmed its political cooperation with PAS and Perikatan Nasional (PN) for the 16th Melaka state election, which will include a joint election manifesto between Barisan Nasional (BN) and PN.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the decision was made at the party’s supreme council meeting yesterday.
He said Umno had directed all its election machinery and supporters to give their full backing to PN candidates contesting in the state election.

“(The meeting) unanimously agreed to formalise the political cooperation and understanding with our strategic partner PAS and our friends from Perikatan Nasional to face the 16th Melaka state election.

“We also agreed for BN and PN to launch a joint election manifesto to offer the best service to the people and to continue the excellence in the state’s administration and development that has been achieved so far,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Asyraf Wajdi also called on party leaders and machinery to campaign courteously and ethically throughout the election period.
He said all parties should avoid slander, insults and personal attacks against rival parties to ensure a mature and harmonious campaign.
Separately, he urged the government, particularly the Finance Ministry, to withdraw its directive cancelling projects that involve the people’s interests, especially in Sabah and Sarawak.
He said rural development projects, including road construction and rural water and electricity supply, must continue for the wellbeing and development of local communities.
333e65f3725075aa: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 29 — Allegations regarding the cancellation or reduction of allocations for the rural road projects (JALB) in Sabah and Sarawak by the Madani Government need to be examined based on accurate facts and information, said the Sabah PKR Leadership Council chairman Datuk Mustapha Sakmud.
In this regard, he suggested that any party raising the matter should provide detailed information, including an official list of projects, allocation values and their implementation status.

Mustapha, who is also the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak Affairs), said that the directive to postpone the issuance of new Letters of Acceptance (SST) dated September 10 was an internal financial control measure to prevent the increase of contract commitments exceeding the annual ceiling and not the cancellation of approved development projects.

“The fact is, the original allocation for JALB at the national level continues to increase from RM2.11 billion for the year 2026 to RM2.27 billion for the year 2027, compared to the previous era which never reached RM1 billion before Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s administration initiated an allocation of RM1.09 billion in 2023.

“In fact, the Ministry of Finance has approved an additional expenditure of RM500 million in 2026 to help address the backlog of payments to JALB contractors to ensure the commitments of existing projects can be fulfilled,” he said.
He said this after chairing a special coordination meeting of the Kota Kinabalu Disaster Committee at Kota Kinabalu City Hall here today.

Mustapha said the federal government’s continued commitment to the development of the Borneo region is reflected in Budget 2027, which allocates RM18.7 billion to Sabah compared to RM17.6 billion previously, while the allocation for Sarawak is increased from RM15.1 billion to RM16.2 billion.

“Meanwhile, an amount of RM3.3 billion has also been allocated specifically for the implementation of road projects in Sabah and Sarawak, covering the continuation of the development of strategic road networks,” he also said.

He emphasised that the development of basic facilities in Sabah and Sarawak remains a long-term investment priority of the Madani Government to strengthen connectivity and bridge the gap between regions. — Bernama
bf3bb7a05c2093d7: PETALING JAYA: Angkatan Tentera Malaysia (ATM) memutuskan untuk menghentikan penjualan bir bebas cukai di premis yang dikendalikan cabang perdagangannya, Pernama, sekali gus menamatkan amalan yang berlangsung selama lebih enam dekad.

Seorang pengurus di premis Pernama, yang enggan namanya didedahkan, berkata pengendali premis baru-baru ini menerima arahan daripada pejabat panglima ATM supaya menghentikan penjualan sebaik sahaja stok sedia ada habis.
Tiada alasan diberikan berhubung keputusan itu.
Menurut pengurus berkenaan, Pernama, yang mempunyai kira-kira 80 premis di seluruh negara, turut diarahkan supaya tidak membuat pesanan baharu, yang lazimnya dilakukan setiap enam bulan.
Pengurus itu berkata stok semasa dijangka habis menjelang akhir tahun ini.
Di bawah peraturan semasa, anggota tentera dan veteran bukan Islam boleh membeli sehingga dua kotak bir setiap bulan daripada Pernama, dengan setiap kotak mengandungi 48 tin atau botol.
Seorang bekas anggota tentera, yang enggan dikenali berkata harga bir yang dibeli daripada Pernama lazimnya kira-kira 60% lebih murah berbanding di premis runcit biasa.
Pernama dimiliki sepenuhnya oleh Lembaga Tabung Angkatan Tentera, sebuah badan berkanun di bawah Kementerian Pertahanan.
Selain produk alkohol, premis itu turut menjual peralatan elektrik bebas cukai, dengan setiap anggota tentera layak membeli satu barangan elektrik sepanjang tempoh perkhidmatan.
Ketika dihubungi, jurucakap Pernama mengesahkan bahawa arahan itu dikeluarkan kepada semua premisnya.
“Berhubung alasan di sebalik arahan itu, kami akan mendapatkan penjelasan daripada pejabat perhubungan awam ATM,” kata jurucakap itu kepada FMT.
Jurucakap itu berkata Pernama ditugaskan untuk memastikan anggota tentera dan penerima manfaat yang layak menikmati keistimewaan mereka 'selaras dengan semua arahan dan dasar yang berkaitan'.
Bekas anggota tentera itu berkata beliau dan ramai rakan seperjuangannya kecewa dengan arahan yang dikeluarkan secara tiba-tiba itu.
Katanya, kemudahan bebas cukai berkenaan adalah beberapa keistimewaan yang masih mereka nikmati selepas bertahun-tahun berkhidmat kepada negara.
“Kebanyakan kami hanya minum sekali-sekala dan menikmati minuman dalam kuantiti yang sedikit. Saya sudah berusia 75 tahun dan kesihatan saya baik kerana saya tidak menyalahgunakan alkohol.
“Kementerian Pertahanan mesti menjelaskan keputusan itu,” katanya ketika dihubungi.
FMT menghubungi Kementerian Pertahanan untuk mendapatkan komen.

Awal bulan ini, New Straits Times melaporkan bahawa anggota tentera dan veteran boleh membeli barangan keperluan pada harga diskaun sepanjang tahun di bawah inisiatif baharu Kementerian Pertahanan menerusi Pernama.
Di bawah program itu, mereka layak menikmati diskaun sehingga 30% bagi 308 barangan.
1efb3b773994b1e8: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is maintaining its decision to contest 21 seats in the Melaka state election for now, with any changes subject to a final decision by the coalition’s top leadership.
PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the coalition will concentrate on the seats that have already been announced.

“We have announced 21 seats. If there are any changes, we leave it to the leadership to announce,” he told reporters at a Deepavali contribution event for the Lembah Pantai parliamentary constituency at IWK Eco Park @ Pantai Dalam last night.
Fahmi said PH will evaluate its participation in the state polls based on its own capacity and capabilities, taking into account strategic and tactical considerations.
“We know several other parties will announce their candidates tomorrow. That is their prerogative, but our considerations are grounded in Pakatan Harapan’s own capabilities,” he said.
Media reports previously indicated that PH was poised to contest three additional seats in the election, with PKR allocated one more seat and Amanah two.
If finalised, the move would see PH contest 24 of the 28 state seats in Melaka. — Bernama
c59b8328aa59deda: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The seat allocation issue within Barisan Nasional (BN) involving component party MCA for the upcoming Melaka state election has been resolved, says Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
He said negotiations had reached an agreement, adding that MCA’s participation as the party representing the Chinese community within BN would be refined and enhanced.

“MCA is okay, settled. Done deal. MCA accepts it as it is, and MCA’s participation representing the Chinese community will certainly be refined and enhanced, Insya-Allah,” he told reporters after attending an UMNO Supreme Council meeting at Menara Dato’ Onn here last night.
Commenting on matters discussed during the meeting, Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Chief Minister, said party machinery had been directed to focus election work on the 21 state seats BN is contesting.
He said State Executive Council members appointed as mentors for specific constituencies have also been tasked with assisting the Melaka BN machinery to secure victory across all contested seats.
“Every vote is crucial for us to defend the 21 seats we are contesting,” he said.
Ab Rauf confirmed that an understanding with BN component parties on election ground operations had been finalised.
Yesterday, Ab Rauf and MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong broke the impasse over seat allocations for the Melaka state election scheduled for next month.
Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka BN election director, described the outcome of the discussions as positive.
MCA had previously stated it would not recognise any party candidates announced by BN for the Melaka polls without the endorsement of its top leadership.
Last Saturday, BN announced its candidates for 21 state seats, including two from MCA, namely Machap Jaya incumbent Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem and Kelebang incumbent Datuk Lim Ban Hong.
Nomination day for the Melaka state election is scheduled for this Saturday, while early voting and polling day have been set for November 10 and 14, respectively. — Bernama
4465b1d4cf3060e0: KUALA LUMPUR: The Coalition for Clean and Fair Elections (Bersih) has criticised Transport Minister Anthony Loke for announcing a RM1,000 special financial assistance for taxi drivers during a Pakatan Harapan candidate announcement event for the Melaka election.
The Bersih steering committee said the move could create the perception that the aid was a contribution from a contesting party, even though it was funded by government revenue.
It said government-funded assistance should not be announced or promoted at political campaign events, as it could provide an unfair advantage to the ruling party.
"Proceeds from the sale of special registration numbers used to fund this aid are government revenue that should rightfully benefit all citizens.
"It is not money belonging to any political party and should not be announced or promoted during campaign events to give an advantage to the ruling party," Bersih said in a statement.
Bersih said explanations that the assistance was meant for recipients nationwide did not address why the aid for Melaka drivers was highlighted during the PH candidate announcement ceremony.
Loke had previously denied that the RM1,000 special aid for taxi, rental car, and school bus drivers in Melaka was aimed at fishing for votes in the state polls.

He said the incentive was being provided to all taxi, rental car, and school bus drivers nationwide, as announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the tabling of the 2027 Budget in parliament recently.S
The aid is funded by proceeds from the sale of the special "H" vehicle registration numbers, which recorded a total collection of RM91.21 million.
Revenue from the sales was channelled into several public initiatives, including the MyLesen Programme, free motorcycle helmets, and financial assistance for taxi and rental car drivers.
495f4b7ac567e2b6: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Police detained three local men and seized 376.2kg of pangolin scales worth an estimated RM376,200 in an integrated operation at a premises in Negeri Sembilan on Tuesday.

The operation, which began at 12.30pm, was carried out by the Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence Division (WCB/PSK) of Bukit Aman’s Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA), in collaboration with the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan), under Operasi Bersepadu Khazanah (OBK).

In a statement yesterday, Bukit Aman WCB/PSK JKDNKA Commander SAC Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said police found 15 boxes of pangolin scales during a search of the premises, suspected to be linked to the storage and distribution of products derived from protected wildlife.
“Other items seized during the operation included nine mobile phones of various brands, a weighing scale and a padlock.

“The total value of the seizure, including other items, is estimated at RM401,700,” he said, adding that police took all suspects and seized items to the Nilai District Police Headquarters before handing them over to Perhilitan investigators for further action.
Mohd Zaki said the case was being investigated under Section 68 of the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010 (Act 716), relating to offences involving wildlife, its parts or derivatives.

“This large-scale seizure underscores the importance of continued intelligence and enforcement operations to combat networks involved in storing, collecting and distributing products derived from wildlife,” he said.

Mohd Zaki said the division had carried out 288 raids nationwide between Jan 1 and today, involving various offences, including wildlife smuggling, untaxed goods, leakage of controlled and subsidised goods, and e-waste-related activities that resulted in 471 arrests, with the total value of seizures estimated at RM350.35 million.
He said 66 cases were recorded this year, involving 74 arrests and seizures worth an estimated RM99.70 million under the OBK. — Bernama
9574e728f0627939: SINGAPORE, Oct 29 — After a career spanning decades, Aamir Khan has made a name for himself, but not without regrets.

The 61-year-old Bollywood star was in town on Oct 22 for the annual Singapore International Film Festival (SGIFF), where he received the Screen Icon Award and chatted with viewers here for nearly two hours during his In Conversations With session.
On top of a look-back at his journey as an actor, director and producer, Aamir also opened up about one of his lowest moments.
Sitting around at home during the Covid-19 pandemic, after being a workaholic all his life, gave him time to reflect.

“About 30 years of my life had passed — and it’s okay to work like a madman, completely obsessed with what you’re doing, for one year, two years, five years, but if it goes on for 30 years… You’ve lost your relationships. Your kids have grown up, they are adults now, so I felt a deep sense of loss,” he shared.
Tearing up, Aamir, who has three children from his two previous marriages, paused for a few moments to collect himself.
“I was sitting alone and thinking about this, feeling really horrible about myself. And then I decided to correct what I had done or what I had not done,” he said.

“I realised that I’ve lost those years, and no matter what I do, they’re not going to come back. There’s no way those years are coming back, but at least I have the years ahead. So I made a big change in my life.”
He shared that he’s been spending time with his loved ones in recent years and is actively making sure he’s “connected” to the people who are important to him.
“I’m so glad that this thought occurred to me when I was 56, and not when I was 86, when it would be really too late to do anything about it.”

He added: “A lot of us have so many things happening in our lives. We are doing so many things that are important to us, which mean a lot to us, and life just races. But I think it’s very important for all of us to just stop, take a pause, and look at the people and our relationships, who are really important to us, and who mean a lot to us, and we must give them time, love and nourish those relationships.”
‘This is where my heart belongs’

Aamir has starred in countless beloved films and dramas — Mann (1999), Dil Chahta Hai (2001), Ghajini (2008) and Dangal (2016), to name a few — but arguably he’s best known for the global hit that is 3 Idiots.
The 2009 movie was popular not only in India, but also in countries such as China and South Korea.
Speaking candidly, Aamir’s next remark drew a surprised reaction from Singaporean host Rishi Budhrani.

“I have to thank piracy. I mean, it’s the truth. My popularity in China is thanks to piracy… Had the Chinese kids not pirated the film and shared it, I don’t think I would have got that out,” he remarked.
He clarified he’s not an advocate of piracy and likes to pay for what he consumes but is aware of the practicalities.

“Sometimes things which are not good for you work in your favour in odd ways. This is one case of that… The first time I went to China, I met a lot of film people there and I realised that they had seen seven, eight films of mine,” he said.
For fans of 3 Idiots, all hope for a sequel is not lost as Aamir confirmed at SGIFF that it is in the works.
Earlier this year, director Rajkumar Hirani revealed he’s working on the script and Aamir said the story picks up 10 years after the first film.
Aamir, whose father was also a film producer, was asked if he envisioned himself taking a different career path.
The former started Aamir Khan Productions in 2001 and its first film Lagaan: Once Upon a Time in India (2001) — which was screened at SGIFF — was a commercial success.

“If I was not an actor, I think I would still be in the film [industry]. I would probably be a filmmaker, producer or editor… Because I think this is where I belong. This is where my heart belongs,” he said.
SGIFF will run until November 1. — AsiaOne
68daebf49a86fd38: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is still investigating Retirement Fund Incorporated’s (KWAP) investment in Indonesian aquaculture technology company eFishery, the Ministry of Finance (MoF) said yesterday.
The ongoing investigation has not uncovered any evidence of criminal wrongdoing involving corruption or misappropriation, as reported by the media on August 13, 2026, the ministry said.
KWAP has also cooperated with relevant authorities and the investor consortium in taking appropriate action against those responsible, MoF added.
“At the same time, efforts are continuing through appropriate channels to maximise the recovery of the investment value,” it said in a written reply on the Parliament website yesterday.
MoF was responding to a question from Tuan Kalam Salan (PN-Sabak Bernam), who wanted to know KWAP’s investment of about RM200 million in eFishery.

Tuan Kalam also requested clarification on the investment approval, the parties responsible for the due diligence failure, total losses, and whether KWAP will take action against the negligent, MoF said.

The eFishery investment underwent established assessment and governance processes, including verification by a qualified international auditor based on the information available at the time, MoF said.
The company was, however, subsequently found to have engaged in financial manipulation and misrepresentation of facts in its financial reports.

“The assessment process before investment approval also included internal evaluations, independent due diligence, and reviews of financial, legal and operational aspects. Several major global institutional investors were also affected by the misconduct,” the ministry said.
The actual investment amounted to RM163.4 million, a 2.51 per cent equity stake.
KWAP is a minority shareholder in eFishery. Other investors, including major global institutional investors, hold most of the company’s shares, it added. — Bernama
9513df4dd22de19f: MOSCOW: Discussions on the US lifting sanctions on Russia's flagship investment fund are underway with the administration of US President Donald Trump, Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov was quoted as saying on Wednesday.
Ushakov, quoted by Russian news agencies, said the head of the Russia Direct Investment Fund, Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev, was actively pursuing talks on lifting the sanctions.
"This conversation is going on. It has been going on for a while. I don't know what the outcome will be," Ushakov was quoted as saying.
"Dmitriev is active in his contacts and that's why the issue is under discussion. It already got into the media a few days ago and discussions are still proceeding."
The New York Times reported earlier in the day that the Trump administration was considering abandoning the sanctions.
Washington has made concessions to Moscow in terms of sanctions imposed following Russia's February 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

Earlier this month, Trump announced that Russia would provide diesel for the US and world markets, temporarily lifting sanctions on Russian fuel. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said on Tuesday that a fourth tanker of diesel would depart on Wednesday.

Trump also issued an executive order waiving key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs including duties on the country's goods and penalties for buying its oil and gas, that had been scheduled to go into effect under the legislation known as the Graham Act that he signed into law last month.
52439df2a7e2939c: GUA MUSANG, Oct 29 — The General Operations Force (GOF) has seized a lorry carrying 25 metric tonnes of Super Import white rice suspected to have been smuggled in from Thailand, during an operation in Paloh here last night.
Sinar Harian reported that the rice and the lorry seized in the 11pm operation, codenamed Op Taring Wawasan, were worth an estimated RM550,000 in total.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said personnel on patrol spotted a suspicious lorry near Kampung Pangkal Senor, along the Kota Bharu-Gua Musang highway.
He said the lorry was stopped for inspection by the roadside of Jalan Bentong-Kota Bharu, in front of a building.
“The inspection found that the lorry was carrying Super Import white rice suspected to have been smuggled from Thailand.

“The driver produced two copies of invoices to explain the source and destination of the rice, but there were doubts over the delivery location stated in the documents,” he told reporters this morning.
Ahmad Radzi said this led to the arrest of the 38-year-old driver to assist in investigations.
He said the lorry, the entire load of rice and the two invoices were seized and handed over to the Kelantan office of the National Paddy and Rice Regulatory (KPB) for further action.

“Initial checks found that the delivery location stated in the invoices was inaccurate, raising suspicion that the documents were used to mislead the authorities about the true source and purpose of the shipment.
“However, the authenticity of the documents is still under investigation,” he was quoted as saying.

According to the Malay daily, Ahmad Radzi said investigations would be widened to identify the source of supply, those who prepared and used the invoices, the transporter, the recipient and the distribution network for the suspected smuggled rice.
The case is being investigated under Section 20 of the Control of Padi and Rice Act 1994.
c4a692bfca5d9ab0: ROME, Oct 29 — Inter reclaimed top spot in Serie A with a nervy 2-0 win at Venezia yesterday, while Samuel Mbangula’s hat-trick inspired Bologna to a 4-2 victory at AC Milan and Juventus stumbled again at Genoa.
Champions Inter drew level with Lazio on 25 points at the top ahead of a hotly anticipated Milan derby meeting with their rivals on Saturday.
Ruben Amorim’s side will go into that game on the back of their first league defeat of the season after Alphadjo Cisse’s double was not enough to avoid a loss that left the Rossoneri fifth.
Inter coach Cristian Chivu admitted that an unconvincing performance was not the perfect derby preparation for his team either.
“We go into that game with eight wins and a draw and are aware that it is a derby,” Chivu told Sky Sport.
“We need to regain mental and physical energy - I’m referring to some of the guys I had to sacrifice at half-time as a wake-up call. If I could have, I would have changed the entire team.”

Fresh off a pulsating stoppage-time turnaround against Fiorentina on Sunday that marked their fifth comeback win of the season, Inter thought they would have to fight back from behind once again when Lion Lauberbach fired home, but he was offside.

Venezia have picked up just three points all season but looked the likelier to make the breakthrough as Ivan Provedel diverted a shot onto the bar before Akor Adams rounded Provedel to score, only for the offside flag to save Inter again.

However, Matias Moreno and Redouane Halhal diverted dangerous deliveries into their own net in the space of two minutes to ensure Inter returned to the top of the standings and Venezia remained rooted to the bottom.
Mbangula magic downs Milan
At San Siro, a lengthy injury list featuring the likes of Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira and Mario Gila restricted Amorim’s options for the first midweek round of the season.
Mbangula, making his full debut for Bologna, swept home the opener inside eight minutes, but the visitors were soon pegged back when an Arthur Theate error gifted Cisse a simple finish.

The Milan teenager struck again in the 27th minute, volleying home a Fikayo Tomori cross, but the game was turned on its head once again in the space of two second-half minutes to stun the San Siro crowd.
The unfortunate Davide Bartesaghi turned a free-kick into his own net before Mbangula struck again with a composed finish in the box just after the hour mark.
The 22-year-old then completed a memorable night when he beat Mike Maignan for a third time.
“A lot of games, a lot of players out,” Amorim told DAZN.

“I felt from the first minute that the team was a little bit tired and without much energy. We conceded two goals quickly; we tried to come back, and we had a great opportunity with (Francesco) Camarda. This number of games was hard for us, with so many players out.”
Juventus slip up again
Juventus’s shaky start continued with a 2-0 defeat away to Genoa, while Napoli thrashed Monza 4-1.
Luciano Spalletti’s inconsistent side have not won back-to-back league games since the opening two weeks of the season and were deservedly beaten at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris.
Kingsley Ehizibue struck early with an angled strike before Tommaso Baldanzi doubled Genoa’s lead in the 28th minute.
Next up for the Turin club is the visit on Sunday of Napoli, who dispatched Monza to go sixth, level on 14 points with Juve.
Head coach Massimiliano Allegri was suspended after being sent off during a 3-3 draw with Roma, but Napoli produced their biggest win of the season in his absence.

Rasmus Hojlund’s early opener was cancelled out by Serie A top scorer Gustavo Varela’s clever header just before the break, while there were concerns when Napoli midfielder Stanislav Lobotka was stretchered off.
Napoli pulled away in the second half as Matteo Politano, Rafa Marin and substitute Kevin De Bruyne struck.
Elsewhere, Adrian Bernabe had a penalty saved by Maduka Okoye as struggling Parma and Udinese played out a 0-0 draw. — AFP
883754d3b0d62fe2: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar today, supported by the possibility of overnight policy rate (OPR) normalisation at Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting next week.

67076228d037f5db: KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry's plans to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) literacy into the school curriculum, Malaysia's participation as a BRICS partner country and the drafting of an AI Governance Bill are among the key topics to be addressed in the Dewan Rakyat today.

0f4fd9efc85d6a79: TODAY, whenever anyone speaks of the beautiful sounds of the sape — Borneo's stylish traditional lute — one Sarawakian immediately comes to mind: Alena Murang.
The 37-year-old musician, who is of Kelabit, British and Italian descent from Kuching, is a passionate advocate for traditional Bornean music.
She believes this ancient art form can elevate world music when paired with modern technology.
Always optimistic that traditional sape music will soon break into the mainstream, Alena reveals that her musical journey started with a very different instrument.
"While I'm a pioneer musician in my family, we are pretty much music lovers. I actually learnt the guitar first when I was 8, graduating to the sape two years later," Alena said in an interview.
When asked if learning the guitar was a prerequisite to playing the sape, she clarified: "No, it's not necessary. Many sape players went straight into it, and I guess I'm just one of the exceptions."
MASTER OF THE STRINGS
Alena admits the sape shares some similarities with the guitar.
"I play and sing at the same time, but I've also performed instrumental pieces with the Malaysian Philharmonic Orchestra (MPO).
"Unlike the guitar, the sape needs a gentler picking. As a result, not many people who play the guitar can master it."
Fortunately, she notes that more young people in Borneo are discovering the instrument's magic.

"I guess I'm one of the new generation's pioneers, and I'm lucky to have joined Womex (World Music Expo — an international world music support and development project based in Berlin) and networked with international music and concert promoters to expand my reach. Networking is the key to making your voice or sound heard."
Today, Alena owns eight sapes and strictly follows the traditional playing style tribal elders taught her.
She notes that audiences at home and abroad react differently to her performances.
"People abroad want to know more about the sape's background, so I share lots of interesting information about it."
HISTORY, HEALING AND BREAKING TABOOS

Alena is remarkably knowledgeable about the history of her instrument. She notes that before the 20th century, the sape was played strictly by men, primarily within Orang Ulu sub-groups such as the Kenyah, Kayan and Kelabit, with the Kenyah widely recognised as its creators.
Beyond its cultural roots, the instrument had a spiritual purpose. In ancient times, it was played during shamanic rituals to heal the sick.

"The belief has long faded away, and the sape is now used to accompany dances or musical performances," she said, noting with pride that she was one of the first Sarawakian women to break the gender taboo.
She also highlights the instrument's close connection to other regional traditions, such as Sabah's long-necked sundatang.
"They have the same scaling, and I hope it will make its own mark on the Malaysian music map one day."
When choosing an instrument, Alena, who is also a talented painter, explains that the wood, body size and strings all dictate the sound.
"We must approach sape as a whole to find which one fits us best. Your instrument is like your beloved pet, and you must take good care of it."
As for the personality of her sapes?
"They are quite sassy and sensitive to temperature, particularly humidity," she laughed.
FROM SCREEN SOUNDTRACKS TO SYMPHONIES
Over the past few years, Alena has expanded into writing music for television and films, including the Prime Video fantasy series 'The Wheel of Time'.
"During the Covid-19 lockdown, creating music for television and movie soundtracks kept me busy, including work on 'The Wheel of Time'," she recalled.
While open to scoring a full feature film, she admitted: "Truth be told, I'm more into purely musical programmes rather than movie soundtracks. But it would be great if I were given the chance."
Her stage performances have reached extraordinary heights.

For her upcoming Concerto for Sape and Orchestra at Dewan Filharmonik Petronas (DFP) on Oct 31, she will perform alongside 60 musicians from the MPO — an experience she describes as "truly great and memorable".

"Playing with the MPO has always been a dream for me, so getting to perform with them again is a great privilege. I've noticed how beautifully the oboes and bassoons blend with the sape," she said of the specially commissioned 20-minute piece by Sabah-born composer Vivian Chua, which will make its world premiere at the concert.
INTERNATIONAL ACCLAIM AND FUTURE DREAMS
Alena's self-taught mastery has earned her global recognition.

Holding a degree in management from the University of Manchester's Business School, her breakthrough came in 2021 when her visually stunning music video for 'Warrior Spirit' won Best Music Video at the Buenos Aires Music Video Festival.
This followed her 2020 award for Best Styling for 'Midang Midang' (filmed in the Bario Highlands), which was nominated for Best International Video alongside pop icon Madonna.

She followed these successes with 'Put Burui' in 2022, 'Pemung Jae' (Trio Version) in 2024 — learnt from sape master Mathew Ngau Jau — and a Silver Medal at the Global Music Awards earlier this year for her Kelabit-language track 'Sekunuh Kamih' (Our Stories).
Alena has an exciting lineup of prospective projects.
Her dream international collaborator is Norwegian singer Aurora Aksnes.
"We both love traditional music that's close to nature. I've seen her performances, and they greatly mesmerise me," she said.
Locally, she hopes to reunite with Sabahan singers Velvet Aduk and Marsha Milan Londoh following their successful "Sounds of Borneo" performance at DFP.
She is also keen to collaborate with fellow Sarawakian artist Belle Sisoski, praising her "amazing with her musicianship".
"Come next year, I've got a first in the works — collaborating with Orang Asli musicians. I also plan to write some songs in Malay."
And if her sape could talk, what would it reveal about her?
"Well, that I get nervous before interviews, listen to upbeat music, and I'm basically a quiet person."
She also added one last surprise about her musical tastes.
"If there's one style of music that people would be completely surprised to hear played on a sape, it's electronic dance music. I love it!"
As for where she hopes her trusty instrument will take her next, her dream performance destination is simple: "All over Japan."
For more details and tickets on the "Beats of Borneo: Alena Murang" with the MPO concert at DFP on Oct 31, visit www.mpo.com.my.
