0461756108b67387: PETALING JAYA: A discarded coffee sachet might seem worthless to most, but Richard Ng sees the makings of a bag.
With patience, a pair of scissors in hand and a little ingenuity, the 68-year-old Ipoh native transforms plastic packaging into colourful woven bags, tissue holders and other useful household items.
His creations are more than a craft project. They reflect a larger mission to reduce plastic waste while showing communities that the things they throw away may still have value.
“I was not always an environmentalist but somebody has to do this,” he said of his work, which began almost by accident.

The 68-year-old, who holds a PhD in business administration and spent 17 years with Open University Malaysia, said it all started when his daughter returned from university with two big bags of mineral water bottles.
“I asked her what she was doing with them, and she told me she was collecting them for recycling,” the grandfather of two said.

The idea stayed with him. In 2014, when a dengue outbreak in Perak's Kinta district prompted an anti-dengue campaign, Ng and his NGO, Ipoh City Watch, discovered 22 illegal dumping sites in Jelapang Tambahan.
“We decided to educate the public not to throw garbage. So how do we educate them? Let's start with a recycling project,” he recalled.
Residents were encouraged to bring in recyclable materials in exchange for cash. The project ran for two years, but Ng realised there was a limit to what conventional recycling could achieve.
“Nobody will buy plastic bottles. They may pay 40 sen per kilo, but if you bring back two big bags, maybe you get less than RM1. Who is going to collect all this for less than a ringgit?”
The problem nagged at him. Then, in 2019, while working in Bangi, he began looking through rubbish bins at laundrettes.

“I found a lot of recyclables, including aluminium cans, but I focused on the plastic detergent bags,” said Ng. “They were colourful, and the quality was good. I was thinking, what should we do with these bags?”

He turned to YouTube and found someone weaving plastic packaging into decorative bags. For weeks, he watched tutorials and experimented with the technique. Each day after work, he would clean, dry and cut the packaging before folding it into small units that could be woven together.
His first successful creation, said Ng, was a bag made from coffee sachets, big enough to hold a 500ml bottle. He later used detergent packets to make a tissue holder.
“One bag requires more than 100 pieces of the coffee sachets,” he pointed out. A tissue holder, meanwhile, uses about 11 plastic bags.
The work is time-consuming, but Ng sees every finished product as an opportunity to keep plastic out of landfills.
After retiring in 2019, he began holding workshops in Ipoh, training more than 100 people, mostly single mothers, to weave discarded materials into products.

He also collects used rice bags from restaurants. Initially, he paid for them; later, he offered to exchange them for biodegradable rubbish bags. Getting people to change their habits, however, remains his biggest challenge.

“Many people say, ‘What you're doing is good’, but they never practise it,” he said. At Kinta Heights, he has found a way to encourage residents to recycle by giving them groceries in exchange for bringing in recyclable items.
The initiative costs money, he says, but the real reward is seeing residents change their behaviour.
“When they see me at my office, they bring the recyclables automatically. I'm very happy that their mindset has changed,” Ng beamed.

He now hopes to revive his weaving workshops and use social media platforms such as TikTok to reach more people. He plans to train participants for free and buy their finished products if they meet his quality standards.
For Ng, the work is ultimately about what this generation leaves behind. He has planted more than 150 trees and teaches schoolchildren about recycling.
“Let's be good ancestors,” he said. “People may not remember who planted the trees, but whatever you planted gives shade and protection.”
b156fb0d412af2a9: PETALING JAYA: The armed forces has decided to stop the sale of duty-free beer at outlets operated by its trading arm, Pernama, ending a practice that has been in place for more than six decades.

A manager at a Pernama outlet, speaking on condition of anonymity, said operators recently received a directive from the office of the armed forces chief instructing them to cease sales once existing stocks are exhausted.
No reason was given for the decision.
According to the manager, Pernama, which has some 80 outlets nationwide, was also told not to place fresh orders, typically made every six months.
The manager said current stocks are expected to run dry by the end of the year.
Under current regulations, non-Muslim servicemen and veterans may purchase up to two crates of beer monthly, each containing 48 cans or bottles, from Pernama.
An ex-serviceman, who also requested anonymity, said beer purchased from Pernama is typically about 60% cheaper than at regular retail outlets.
Pernama is fully owned by the Armed Forces Fund Board, a statutory body under the defence ministry.
Besides alcohol products, the outlets also sell duty-free electrical appliances, with each serviceman entitled to purchase one such item during their career.
When contacted, a Pernama spokesman confirmed that the directive had been issued to all of its outlets.
“As for the reasons behind the directive, we will seek an explanation from the Malaysian Armed Forces public relations office,” the spokesman told FMT.
The spokesman said Pernama is tasked with ensuring military personnel and eligible beneficiaries enjoy their privileges “in accordance with all relevant directives and policies”.

The ex-serviceman said he and many of his peers were disappointed by the sudden directive, describing the duty-free benefit as one of the few privileges they continue to enjoy after years of service to the nation.
"Most of us are casual drinkers who enjoy small amounts occasionally. I am already 75 years old and I am okay health wise as I don't abuse alcohol.
"The defence ministry must explain its decision,” he said when contacted.
FMT has reached out to the defence ministry for comment.

Earlier this month, the New Straits Times reported that military personnel and veterans would be able to purchase essential goods at discounted prices throughout the year under a new initiative by the defence ministry through Pernama.
Under the programme, they are entitled to discounts of up to 30% on 308 items.
114d35dfa5aa303d: PETALING JAYA: Seramai 5,000 pelajar B40 di Johor akan menerima pek SIM prabayar Yes 5G berserta 50GB data internet percuma menerusi inisiatif digerakkan atas keprihatinan Raja Permaisuri Agong Raja Zarith Sofiah terhadap pendidikan dan kebajikan generasi muda.

Sumbangan bernilai RM100,000 itu disalurkan YTL Communications Sdn Bhd menerusi Inisiatif Kesalinghubungan Digital Johor dengan kerjasama Yayasan Raja Zarith Sofiah Negeri Johor (YRZSNJ) dan Jabatan Pendidikan Negeri Johor.

Inisiatif itu turut mengambil kira keperluan pelajar susulan keadaan jerebu yang melanda negara baru-baru ini, khususnya bagi memastikan proses Pengajaran dan Pembelajaran di Rumah (PdPR) dapat diteruskan dengan lebih lancar.
Setiap pek SIM dilengkapi 50GB data internet berkelajuan tinggi secara percuma bagi memudahkan pelajar mengakses bahan pendidikan digital dan mengikuti pembelajaran dari rumah.
Sumbangan itu disampaikan Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif YTL Communications Wing K Lee kepada Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif YRZSNJ Hishammuddin Abdul Rahim, semalam.
Hishammuddin berkata sumbangan itu dapat membantu merapatkan jurang digital dalam kalangan keluarga B40 yang berdepan kekangan akses internet.
Menurutnya, kemudahan berkenaan juga dapat memastikan pelajar mengikuti PdPR dengan lebih lancar dan berkesan.
Sementara itu, Wing berharap pengagihan pek SIM percuma itu dapat membantu pelajar di Johor supaya tidak ketinggalan dalam pembelajaran.
Turut hadir Timbalan Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif YTL Communications Jacob Yeoh Keong Yeow, Ketua Pemasarannya Chay Wan Nee dan Pengurus Komunikasi Korporat YRZSNJ Dawson Yeang.
de1c44dac91ab899: MADRID: The death toll from a collision between two high-speed trains in central Spain rose to at least 68 on Wednesday, as prime minister Pedro Sanchez pledged a thorough investigation into the disaster, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
Speaking at the crash site in Urda, Toledo, Sanchez said authorities would determine the cause of the accident and take action if wrongdoing was uncovered, Spanish news agency EFE reported.
"We will get to the bottom of this. If there has been negligence, it will be known," he said.
Sanchez announced three days of national mourning from Oct 29 to 31, saying it was "unacceptable for a country like Spain" to experience two high-speed rail accidents in a single year.
He referred to another train crash in Adamuz, Cordoba, in January.

The prime minister said preliminary indications suggested the two accidents had different causes, but stressed that determining this was the responsibility of independent investigators and judicial authorities.
He pledged decisive measures to restore public confidence in Spain's railway system if safety shortcomings were identified.

Meanwhile, opposition People's Party leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo demanded "immediate" government and judicial investigations, insisting they be conducted "with all available resources and without interference."
Feijoo said Spain "has the right to know what is happening with its infrastructure," calling for a comprehensive, independent review of the country's entire railway network.
He declined to discuss political responsibility for the disaster, saying it was not the day to do so.

A minute of silence will be held at 8pm local time (1900GMT) on Wednesday at town halls across Spain to honour the victims, according to the Spanish Federation of Municipalities and Provinces, which organised the tribute.
487411e9b91baa10: KUALA LUMPUR: The Federal Territory Islamic Religious Department (Jawi) has introduced tiered burials at the Raudhatul Sakinah Islamic Cemetery in Kepong to optimise limited burial space.

The pilot project is being implemented by the department's Mosque Management Division in collaboration with the Dakwah Management Division and the Kuala Lumpur Public Works Department (PWD), specifically for unclaimed bodies.
Jawi said the initiative also introduces a pulley machine developed by Kuala Lumpur PWD to lower bodies to a depth of eight feet.
"In addition, to ensure structural safety, trench boxes are used to prevent soil collapse during the tiered burial process," Jawi said in a statement.
The department hopes the equipment will improve burial efficiency and assist ground personnel.
"Efforts to improve and upgrade the operations of Islamic cemeteries, including exploring suitable technologies and equipment, aim to ensure Jawi's services are delivered effectively.
"This effort also reflects the department's commitment to ensuring funeral management is carried out responsibly, orderly and respectfully in accordance with Islamic requirements," it said.
1473a913dc86e080: KUALA LUMPUR: A series of cryptic social media posts by actress Fasha Sandha has left fans guessing about the current state of her relationship with her younger sister, fellow actress Elisya Sandha.

The 42-year-old star, whose real name is Nur Fasha Sandha Hassan, recently took to her Instagram Story to ask her followers for their thoughts on dealing with family members who fail to keep their word.
"Family is everything. If you make a promise, you should keep it, right?" she wrote.
"Have your own siblings ever broken a promise to you? Is it acceptable to feel aggrieved with siblings, or are second children always expected to yield?"
She added: "Who here is a second child? Second children are truly the best because of their patience, aren't they?"
Her posts appeared to trigger a response from Elisya via a separate update on Threads.
Expressing her frustration, Elisya shared: "I rarely write things like this, but I am deeply hurt. Is a younger sibling always expected to back down?"
"Just because you are the elder sister, do you think you can say whatever you like to hurt someone's feelings? Having an elder sister like this is completely pointless!" she added.
Despite the intense exchange, neither actress named specific individuals in their respective posts.
The online drama quickly caught widespread attention, though many social media users questioned whether the apparent rift was real or merely a publicity stunt for an upcoming television project.
"It is impossible for Elisya and Fasha to be fighting. I'm just waiting for the new TV3 drama," one commenter noted.
Another user chimed in: "Just reveal the title of the new drama and its release date. God willing, people will still support it."

b47f7433ee2aa733: PETALING JAYA: Parti Rakyat India Malaysia (MIPP) tidak akan menyertai PRN Melaka selepas gagal mencapai persetujuan dengan kepimpinan Perikatan Nasional (PN).
Presiden MIPP, P Punithan, berkata parti itu tidak akan menggadaikan prinsipnya semata-mata untuk mendapatkan kerusi dalam PRN 14 Nov ini.

Tegasnya, perjuangan MIPP adalah mempertahankan kepentingan masyarakat India dengan penuh bermaruah dan prinsip, selain suara serta kepentingan masyarakat itu wajar mendapat pengiktirafan dan diwakili dalam landskap politik negara.
"Kerusi boleh dicari, tetapi maruah perjuangan kita tidak boleh sesekali dikorbankan," katanya kepada FMT.
"Bagi MIPP, maruah dan prinsip lebih penting daripada mengejar kerusi tidak relevan. Kami tidak akan mengorbankan prinsip demi kepentingan politik semata-mata.
"MIPP bukan parti yang akan berkompromi hanya untuk menjadi calon."

Punithan berkata, kerjasama berpasukan, sikap saling menghormati serta keterangkuman adalah elemen penting dalam mana-mana gabungan politik, di mana pakatan yang kuat mesti dibina atas dasar kepercayaan dan sedia menghormati kepentingan setiap parti komponen.
MIPP tidak memenangi sebarang kerusi ditandinginya menerusi penampilan sulung parti itu pada PRN Johor tahun ini. Semua lima calonnya hilang wang deposit.
Rabu lalu, Pengerusi Barisan Nasional (BN), Zahid Hamidi dilaporkan berkata, gabungan itu akan bertanding 21 daripada 28 kerusi DUN Melaka, manakala PAS dan sekutunya bertanding baki tujuh kerusi.
Pengumuman itu menyusul spekulasi selama berminggu-minggu berhubung kemungkinan BN dan PN membentuk pakatan pada PRN Melaka.
Setiausaha Agung PAS, Takiyuddin Hassan dilaporkan berkata, pembahagian kerusi belum dimuktamadkan, tetapi tegasnya kerjasama antara dua gabungan itu akan diteruskan.
Penamaan calon bagi PRN Melaka akan diadakan Sabtu ini, dengan pengundian awal ditetapkan pada 10 Nov dan hari pengundian pada 14 Nov nanti.
Pada PRN Melaka 2021, BN memenangi 21 daripada 28 kerusi, manakala Pakatan Harapan lima kerusi dan PN dua kerusi.
a28ef6d9983695c7: ISTANBUL: Google announced its latest artificial intelligence (AI) model, Gemini 4 Carbon, on Wednesday, claiming significant gains in coding, autonomous agent tasks and cybersecurity defence, Anadolu Ajansi reported.

Unveiled just two weeks after the launch of its Gemini 4 Argon model, the company described Carbon in a blog post as its strongest frontier model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities.
Google attributed the rapid release timeline to its researchers and AI models "working hand in hand to advance capabilities faster."
The company claimed that Gemini 4 Carbon ranks first on the updated version 5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 59.

Based on user feedback from its previous release, Google said it improved the model across full-stack web development, scientific tasks and multimodal understanding, claiming an 89-point jump to fourth place on the WebDev Arena leaderboard.

In cybersecurity benchmarks, the tech giant claimed the model holds a "firm lead," scoring 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for finding vulnerabilities, 54.8% on ExploitGym for exploitation and 71% on CWE-bench for patching.

"On internal benchmarks, Carbon drives a strong uplift in generating secure code, and in live coding environments with our own teams it shows reduced misalignment and fabrication rates," the company said.

Addressing safety and alignment, Google claimed that internal testing showed Carbon cuts unsupported claims by approximately half compared to Argon, stating methodological caveats directly rather than fabricating missing evidence.

The company also claimed the model retrieves relevant sources and surfaces discrepancies to users when facing ambiguity, while reducing task overreach by 26% and under-service by 29% during multi-step workflows.
Google said Gemini 4 Carbon will first become available to cybersecurity defenders this week before rolling out more broadly to developers, businesses and consumers.

The company plans to offer introductory pricing of US$2 per 1 million input tokens and US$10 per 1 million output tokens, with cached input tokens discounted by 95%, before standard pricing rises to US$4 per 1 million input tokens and US$20 per 1 million output tokens.
5a2b3c89744c791f: IPOH: Perak State Agricultural Development Corp (Perak SADC) has strengthened its workplace health culture through the Perak SADC Active & Wellness Day 2026 programme.
The event brought together 250 employees from the corporation's headquarters and plantations under its management.
It aimed to encourage an active lifestyle and highlight the importance of work-life balance in creating a healthier and more productive working environment.

Perak SADC chief executive officer Mohd Azhar Mohd Yusof said untreated health problems could affect employees' ability to perform their duties effectively and, in turn, impact organisational productivity.
"Sometimes, we see even young employees facing health problems. That is why we want to cultivate a culture of looking after our health so they can work well and achieve high performance.
"If our mental and physical health is not strong, how can we work towards high performance?" he said.
Azhar was speaking at the programme, themed "Active Together, Well Together", at Dewan Kelarai, Serai Estate, here yesterday.
The programme featured a 5km run and fun walk, free comprehensive health screenings and knowledge-sharing sessions on work-life balance, healthy eating and personal healthcare.

Free screening services included blood pressure monitoring, blood sugar and cholesterol checks, eye examinations, bone density tests, Smart Pulse assessments, body composition analysis and consultations.
The programme also featured interactive quizzes, lucky draws and a blood donation drive in collaboration with Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital.

Azhar said the event received sponsorship and support from the Health Ministry, HTM Pharmacy, Quill Ipoh Orthopaedic Hospital, Sunway Medical Centre Ipoh, Decathlon, Takaful Malaysia, ViQ and Serai Group.
Held in conjunction with National Sports Day, the programme provided an opportunity to boost ties between headquarters staff and employees at Perak SADC-managed plantations across the state.
"It gives plantation management staff an opportunity to interact with senior officers at headquarters. They can also undergo health screenings and donate blood."
Azhar said Perak SADC planned to organise more recreational activities next year to promote healthy living, including hiking and rafting.
"These activities are aimed at safeguarding the health of Perak SADC employees while boosting relationships among colleagues through group recreation."
In a related development, Azhar said the corporation's commitment to employee welfare had been recognised through two awards.
These were the HR Sustainability & Transformation Award 2026 at the Asean HR Excellence Awards 2026 (Malaysia Edition) and the Perak Best Employer Award 2026 from the Employees Provident Fund.

"These awards show that we prioritise employee welfare. Human resources are our most valuable asset because our people are the ones who drive the organisation towards excellence," he said. By Muhammad Zulsyamini Sufian Suri

3ea2dea4251be1a5: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Thursday, supported by the possibility of overnight policy rate (OPR) normalisation at Bank Negara Malaysia Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting next week.
At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.0720/0800 against the US dollar from Wednesday's close of 4.0745/0790.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the unchanged OPR at 2.75 per cent could provide support for the local currency.

Meanwhile, he said the US dollar index (DXY) is currently down by 0.19 per cent to 102.127 points as Federal Open Market Committee members left the benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.75 per cent to four per cent.
"It appears that the Federal Reserve is taking a guarded approach to reach its price stability goal at a time when the economy is deemed to be growing at a robust rate.
"On that note, we foresee the ringgit could be well supported," he told Bernama.
At the open, the ringgit was traded mostly lower against major currencies.

The ringgit gained vis-a-vis the Japanese yen to 2.5798/5851 from 2.5812/5843 at Wednesday's close, but edged down against the British pound to 5.4268/4374 from 5.4130/4190 and fell against the euro to 4.5427/5516 from 4.5337/5387.
The ringgit performed mixed against its Asean peers.
It inched up against the Indonesian rupiah to 223.9/224.4 from 224.0/224.4, while flat against the Philippine peso at 6.36/6.37.
The local note fell against the Singapore dollar to 3.1785/1850 from 3.1775/1813 at Wednesday's close, and was marginally lower against the Thai baht to 12.0759/1068 from 12.0726/0902.
0725c39e32e1e3df: NEW YORK: Nike unveiled on Wednesday its first-ever running shoe designed specifically for India, marking the sportswear giant's latest bid to reach shoppers in the world's most populous country as it grapples with a sales slump in other key regions including China.
The shoe, dubbed Vegam Run, follows Nike's announcement earlier this month that it plans to open a new campus in India, where it is seeking to make inroads amid a running boom.
The running shoe is set to be released on India's e-commerce marketplace Flipkart on November 1, priced at ₹3,795 (RM163). It was developed in about five months, Nike said.

CEO Elliott Hill, two years into his tenure, is betting on a revamped product pipeline to turn around the struggling sportswear juggernaut, which analysts say will hinge in large part on locally led designs in key markets.
Nike is trying to push into India at a time when China, historically a profit driver for the company, continues to show particular weakness.
Sales in China, which account for about fifteen per cent of Nike's annual revenue, have fallen for nine consecutive quarters as international rivals ‌and domestic ⁠sportswear groups gain traction.
Shares have tumbled more than 40 per cent so far this year. But Nike's global running business has emerged as a bright spot, growing by double digits for six consecutive quarters.

"Our Nike performance business is not yet large enough to offset the pressure ​we're seeing in Nike sportswear, Jordan brand, and Greater China," Hill warned analysts this month after the company projected a surprisingly steep drop in full-year revenue. — REUTERS
ae11e943fe8dd0ba: GUA MUSANG: The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 25 tonnes of white rice suspected to have been smuggled from Thailand along Jalan Bentong-Kota Bharu near Paloh here on Tuesday night.
The seizure was made by the Southeast Brigade Commander's special team under Op Taring Wawasan after stopping a lorry at 11pm.
Southeast Brigade GOF commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said an inspection found that the lorry was carrying white rice suspected to have been smuggled from Thailand.
"The lorry driver produced two copies of invoices to explain the source and destination of the rice consignment. However, there were doubts over the delivery location stated in the invoices.
"Following this, the 38-year-old driver was arrested, while the lorry and its 25,000kg rice cargo were seized for further action," he said in a statement.
Ahmad Radzi said the total value of the lorry and rice seized was estimated at RM550,000.
He said the modus operandi involved using suspected fake intermediary invoices to mislead the authorities during inspections and make the shipment appear to be supported by legitimate documents.
"Preliminary checks raised doubts over the delivery location stated in the invoices, as the location provided was inaccurate.
"This raised suspicions that the documents were being used to mislead the authorities about the actual source and destination of the rice consignment.

"Information obtained from the arrest will be further developed to identify the source of supply, those involved in preparing the documents, transporters, recipients and distribution network for the rice suspected to have been smuggled from Thailand," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 20 of the Control of Padi and Rice Act 1994.

1fa36adffa7faac3: GAZA CITY: Gaza's civil defence agency and a local hospital said Israeli strikes killed five people and wounded others in the Palestinian territory on Wednesday.

The war began on Oct 7, 2023, following an unprecedented attack by Hamas on southern Israel that killed 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.
Israel responded with a massive military campaign that has destroyed much of Gaza and killed more than 74,500 people, according to the territory's health ministry.

270aee5ea45a14da: Melihat senarai calon wanita untuk PRN Melaka saya sebetulnya terkedu. Ia cepat membawa saya kepada watak-watak wanita ikonik dalam sejarah Kesultanan Melayu Melaka. Sukar untuk memadam watak-watak seperti Tun Kudu, Tun Teja dan Tun Fatimah dari benak. Malangnya wanita yang saya sebutkan ini dihinjak dalam politik.

Ambil sahaja Tun Kudu yang menjadi sekadar 'alat' untuk kepentingan penguasa. Tun Kudu adalah puteri kepada Bendahara Seri Wak Raja dan merupakan permaisuri kepada Sultan Muzaffar Syah yang memerintah Melaka (1446-1459). Namun demikian untuk meredakan perseteruan dua kem politik orang Melayu yang berebutkan kedudukan sebagai bendahara, Sultan Muzzafar Syah telah menceraikan Tun Kudu dan mengaturkan baginda untuk menjadi isteri Bendahara Seri Nara Diraja yang sudah tua kerepot, lagi berusia.

Seri Nara Diraja memang menyebabkan Sultan Muzaffar sakit kepala kerana enggan bersara, membolot jawatan tersebut setelah Bendahara Seri Wak Raja dan hanya sedia melakukannya dengan syarat diberi hadiah gundik sultan. Makanya dalam percaturan Sultan Muzaffar, Paduka Raja Tun Perak, iaitu kekanda Tun Kudu terpaksa mengambil sikap damai. Tun Ali atau Seri Nara Diraja itu adalah bapa saudara Sultan Muzaffar Syah dan pembesar yang bertanggungjawab mengatur dan meletakkan Sultan Muzaffar di atas takhta pada 1446.

Watak kedua pula adalah Tun Teja iaitu anak Bendahara Pahang Seri Amar Bangsa Diraja dan disebut sebagai tunangan kepada Sultan Pahang, Sultan Abdul Jalil. Akan tetapi Sultan Mahmud Syah yang gila perempuan telah berusaha mendapatkan Tun Teja lantas bertitah kepada pembesar; "Barang siapa membawa anak Bendahara Pahang itu ke mari, apa yang dikehendakinya ku anugerahkan akan dia. Jikalau ia hendakkan sekerat kota dengan kerajaan sekalipun kita anugerahkan".

Dalam riwayat, Tun Teja dilarikan oleh Hang Nadim (menantu kepada Laksamana Hang Tuah) demi menebus kesalahannya terhadap sultan. Untuk melakukannya, Hang Nadim merasuah seorang pelulut untuk memujuk Tun Teja agar kelak berkahwin dengan Sultan Mahmud Syah. Berdasarkan Hikayat Hang Tuah, Tun Teja merupakan seorang yang bermaruah tinggi dan bukanlah gilakan kedudukan. Beliau malah menolak lamaran sultan Melaka, sebaliknya memilih menjadi isteri Megat Panji Alam Terengganu.
Perbuatan pelulut membujuk Tun Teja ini gagal. Oleh sebab Tun Teja liat dan berkeras, malangnya baginda disihir dengan ubat guna-guna lantas dipaksa berkahwin dengan Sultan Mahmud tanpa kerelaan.

Sultan Mahmud Syah selaku raja dan sultan yang gila perempuan seterusnya mensasarkan pula Tun Fatimah. Baginda adalah anak Tun Mutahir dan baru berkahwin dengan Tun Ali. Sultan Mahmud Syah menggunakan kuasa baginda untuk membunuh Tun Ali sebelum merebut Tun Fatimah. Ini juga didorong oleh fitnah Raja Mendaliar kononnya Tun Mutahir sedang merancang untuk menggulingkannya. Sultan menitahkan Tun Sura Diraja dan Tun Indera Segara untuk menghabisi seisi keluarga bendahara. Kesan atau trauma kehilangan seisi keluarga dan suami itu, Tun Fatimah hidup berendam dendam. Dalam riwayat disebut Tun Fatimah itu 'selama ia duduk dengan Sultan Mahmud Syah jangankan ia tertawa, tersenyum pun tiada pernah'. Bahkan setiap kali mengandung, baginda menggugurkan kandungannya.

Kisah raja gila seks, termakan fitnah dan pertelingkahan politik antara kem pembesar untuk berebut kedudukan dan jawatan bendahara ini adalah satu renungan yang penting untuk kita memahami pula konteks semasa.

Hari ini Melaka menyaksikan sekali lagi perebutan kuasa dalam bentuk pilihan raya. Dengan mengambil ingatan, Melaka melayan watak wanita sebagai alat percaturan politik, pemuas nafsu dan sekadar di pinggiran; saya dengan berhati-hati mencari parti politik yang tidak melakukan hal-hal sedemikian. Saya juga menyuruhkan kaum keluarga saya yang terdiri dari pengundi wanita untuk tidak memilih mereka yang melayan wanita dengan buruk.

Sudah tentu kita telah menjauhi era kesultanan Melayu yang penuh malapetaka seperti di atas. Iklim politik kita juga harapnya tidaklah setoksik itu. Pun tenung punya tenung saya mesti memastikan parti politik manakah yang tidak menjadikan wanita sekadar melukut di tepi gantang. Saya benci perlakuan Melaka di zaman lampau tersebut.

Mengapakah saya memberi tumpuan kepada wanita? Jawapan mudahnya, ini adalah kerana dalam rekod, terdapat 348,849 orang pengundi di PRN Melaka kali ini adalah perempuan, iaitu 50.73% daripada jumlah keseluruhan pemilih. Justeru saya berpandangan penting untuk kita melihat komponen parti manakah yang paling bersungguh memperjuangkan wanita.

Letak duduk wanita dalam politik adalah penting terutama setelah ucapan kontroversi di Persidangan Agung Umno 2026, iaitu apabila Presiden Zahid Hamidi berseloroh mengatakan Ketua Wanita Noraini Ahmad nampak macam 'nenek-nenek'.

Pakatan Harapan menjanjikan lima orang calon wanita untuk membawa mandat rakyat Melaka di kawasan masing-masing. Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) mengetengahkan tiga orang calon wanita dalam PRN Melaka, pada 14 November ini. Menurut Setiausaha Agung Fuziah Salleh, daripada sembilan calon yang diketengahkan parti itu, tiga calon wanita telah diberi kepercayaan untuk bertanding, dan ini mewakili 33.3% daripada keseluruhan calon PKR pada PRN. Calon wanita ini adalah Ketua Pemuda Tangga Batu, Farzana Hayani Nasir di Klebang; Ketua Penerangan Wanita Ginie Lim Siew Lin yang sekali lagi bertanding di DUN Machap Jaya, dan Esma Eazreen Husin di Rim. Farzana, seorang Gen Z baru-baru ini mendapat perhatian ramai apabila diusir seorang anggota wanita Umno dari menghadiri program Kampung Angkat Madani di kawasan masjid Bukit Rambai.

Dalam pada itu, Amanah di Merlimau membawakan Rahayu Hamzah. Beliau akan membawa tugas besar untuk menewaskan Ketua Pemuda Umno, Dr Akmal Saleh yang baru-baru ini kalah dalam saman berkaitan isu cadangan pensijilan halal, di mana Akmal merujuk Ahli Parlimen Seputeh, Teresa Kok sebagai 'nyonya tua'. Akmal diperintahkan membayar ganti rugi berjumlah RM250,000 kepada Teresa. Ini termasuklah kos perundangan sebanyak RM50,000 (jumlah keseluruhan RM300,000). Dalam vonis hakim, iaitu Isa Aziz Ibrahim; Akmal malah ditegur dengan kata-kata bahawa adab itu membentuk keperibadian.

481abf92448c2550: PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Indian People’s Party (MIPP) will sit out the Melaka state election after failing to reach an agreement with the Perikatan Nasional (PN) leadership.
MIPP president P Punithan told FMT that the party would not compromise its principles simply to secure seats in the Nov 14 polls.

He said MIPP’s struggle was to defend the interests of the Indian community with dignity and principles, and that the community’s voice and interests deserved proper recognition and representation in the political landscape.
"Seats can be sought, but the dignity of our struggle must never be sacrificed," he said.
"For MIPP, dignity and principles are more important than pursuing irrelevant seats. We will not sacrifice our principles merely for political interests.
"MIPP is not a party that will compromise simply for the sake of becoming candidates."

Punithan said teamwork, mutual respect and inclusiveness were essential to any political coalition, and that a strong alliance must be built on trust and a willingness to respect the interests of every component party.
MIPP won none of the five seats it contested in its electoral debut in Johor this year. All five MIPP candidates lost their deposits.
On Wednesday, Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the coalition would contest 21 of Melaka’s 28 state seats, while PAS and its allies would vie for the remaining seven.
The announcement followed weeks of speculation over a possible electoral pact in Melaka between BN and PN.
However, PAS secretary-general Takiyuddin Hassan said seat distribution had yet to be finalised, although he maintained that cooperation between the parties was certain.
Nomination for the Melaka election will take place on Saturday, with early voting on Nov 10 and polling on Nov 14.
In the 2021 state election, BN won 21 of the 28 seats, while Pakatan Harapan secured five and PN won two.
f9006176b11cc8e6: PETALING JAYA: Electric vehicles may be attracting much of the attention in Malaysia's automotive market, but another form of electrified motoring is enjoying a remarkable resurgence.
Hybrid vehicles, which combine conventional engines with electric technology, have already surpassed their previous annual registration record, with October to December still to be accounted for.
According to road transport department (JPJ) data, 40,181 hybrid vehicles were registered between January and September, representing an 83.1% increase over the corresponding period last year.
The figure comfortably exceeds 2025's full-year record of 31,190 registrations: September alone accounted for 5,448 vehicles, more than double the number recorded during the same month in 2025.

Hybrids represented 7.3% of new vehicle registrations in September, compared with 3.8% a year earlier, reflecting their growing presence in a market still dominated by conventional petrol-powered cars.

For motorists intrigued by electric technology but reluctant to depend entirely on charging infrastructure, these vehicles offer an alternative that retains much of the familiarity of conventional motoring.
Depending on their design, hybrids can use electric power to assist acceleration, recover energy during braking or travel short distances without engaging their petrol engines.

The distinction matters because not all hybrids operate in the same way. Conventional full hybrids recharge their batteries through the engine and regenerative braking, without requiring external charging.
Mild hybrids primarily assist the engine, while plug-in hybrids feature larger batteries that can be charged externally and generally permit longer journeys using electricity alone.

JPJ's registration figures combine these different technologies under the hybrid category, meaning the overall increase reflects demand for several types of vehicles rather than one particular system.
The growing selection of models has also helped broaden their appeal, offering buyers choices across different vehicle segments and price points.

One particularly notable development is the growing contribution of plug-in hybrids. Full hybrids accounted for approximately 59% of registrations during the first nine months of this year, while models sold exclusively as plug-in hybrids contributed another 29%.
The Proton e.MAS 7 PHEV led the hybrid rankings with 6,247 registrations during that period, followed by strong performances from established Japanese manufacturers.

Its popularity illustrates how Malaysian brands are becoming part of the electrification story, although the availability of new models also makes it difficult to attribute the overall growth to any single consumer preference.
Charging convenience remains a consideration, particularly for motorists living in properties without dedicated parking or reliable access to charging facilities.

For some drivers, a conventional hybrid offers improvements in fuel efficiency without requiring changes to their refuelling routine. Plug-in hybrids, meanwhile, provide greater opportunities for electric driving, although their benefits depend partly on how regularly they are charged.
An expanding market, not a replacement

The rise of hybrids does not suggest Malaysians are abandoning fully electric vehicles. EV registrations have also increased substantially this year, indicating that different forms of electrified transport are finding their own audiences.
Indeed, the wider trend points towards a market offering motorists more options between conventional petrol engines and fully electric powertrains.

The financial considerations remain important. Hybrid vehicles may offer fuel savings, but buyers must still weigh purchase prices, maintenance requirements and their individual driving habits before deciding whether the technology represents good value.

What the latest figures demonstrate is that electrification in Malaysia is no longer confined to cars that require plugging in. For an increasing number of motorists, the transition towards electric technology appears to be taking place one hybrid at a time.

cded051db6c4e7f8: WASHINGTON: The US on Wednesday imposed sanctions on the Rwandan defence ministry and a financial institution in that country over their alleged ties to the M23 armed group fighting in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

"Today, the United States makes good on President (Donald) Trump's promise to hold Rwanda accountable for its commitments under the Washington Accords for Peace and Prosperity," said treasury secretary Scott Bessent, referring to an agreement signed in December between Rwandan and DR Congo leaders.
"Rwanda must halt its support for M23 and withdraw its troops from eastern DRC."
With Rwandan help, the M23 movement has seized swathes of the eastern DRC -- home to valuable minerals coveted by world powers -- since it took up arms again in 2021.
Despite the US-brokered truce in December, fighting has continued to rage in a region that has been torn apart by conflict for three decades and faces an Ebola epidemic.
An offensive by the M23 and the Rwandan army in eastern DRC in early 2025 resulted in the capture of Goma and Bukavu, capitals of North and South Kivu provinces.
Since then, the front line has stabilized, though South Kivu in particular has seen fierce clashes.

While UN experts have reported that Rwanda still has thousands of troops helping the M23 and exerts de facto control over the group, the DRC's neighbor has long denied offering the M23 military support.
Rwanda insists that it faces an existential threat from a Congolese militia founded by ethnic Hutus involved in the 1994 genocide of Tutsis in Rwanda.
US state department spokesman Tommy Pigott, however, said that "thousands" of Rwanda Defense Force troops continued to fight alongside M23 in North and South Kivu provinces.

Wednesday's US action included blocking financial transactions with Zigama Credit and Savings Society, the treasury department said, calling it a financial institution that serves Rwanda's security services.
The US sanctioned the Rwanda Defence Force, which falls under the defence ministry, in March.

084be14b2ecb2e41: MANCHESTER: Enzo Maresca admitted Manchester City did not practice penalties at all this season before beating Brighton & Hove Albion in a League Cup fourth round shoot-out on Wednesday.
City goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli made two penalty saves as the League Cup holders won 4-3 in the shoot-out after twice coming from behind in a 2-2 draw at the Etihad Stadium.
Maresca had opted against asking his players to practice penalties in training since his close-season arrival to replace Pep Guardiola.
City's lack of spot-kick preparation was no problem thanks to reserve keeper Rulli, who denied Brighton's Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to send City into the last eight.
Mateo Kovacic did miss from the spot but Phil Foden, Enzo Fernandez, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki were all successful.
"To be honest, since I've been here we never practised penalties," said Maresca, whose side will host third tier Bradford City for a place in the semi-finals.
"We're very happy with the five, even Mateo. It always happens, the one that scored during the 90 minutes, and then misses the penalty."
Kovacic had cancelled out Malick Yalcouye's opener for Brighton before half-time.
Georginio Rutter restored the Seagulls' lead after the restart, but Vitor Reis diverted in a Cherki free-kick to take the match to penalties.
"I'm not sure he changed the game, but for sure he made an impact," said Maresca of Belgian winger Doku.
"This is the reason why they are there – when they start from the beginning, to try to do their best, and if they go on from the bench, to try to make an impact."
City had suffered their first Premier League defeat this season on Saturday, losing at Aston Villa to end their 100 percent start to the top-flight campaign.

It was vital for City to bounce back with a win against Brighton as they try to remain positive while awaiting the verdict in their appeal against a guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules.
If the appeal fails, City could be hit with a massive points deduction that would effectively lead to relegation.
In the midst of a pressure-packed schedule, Maresca had no regrets about his decision to rest Erling Haaland, Gianluigi Donnarumma, Ruben Dias, Elliot Anderson and Josko Gvardiol against Brighton.
"I was happy with the way we planned the game, with the rotation, and especially I was very, very, very happy with the ones that were playing," he said.
Maresca, who made nine changes, praised Donnarumma's deputy Rulli for his composed display.
"Apart from the penalties, I think overall he was good, especially in the build-up. He also made a good save," he said.

e048a2bd1e4547e3: SHAH ALAM: A damp patch on the wall or stain on the ceiling may look like a small nuisance at first - but for some homeowners, it can mark the beginning of a long and costly repair cycle.

A recent Malaysian homeowner survey developed by the Home Buyers Association (HBA) and Nippon Paint Malaysia found that nearly nine in 10 respondents whose defect liability period (DLP) had ended experienced waterproofing problems afterwards.
Among those affected, 42.4% spent more than RM5,000 on repairs, while 14.2% paid over RM10,000.
The bigger frustration is that fixing the problem once may not be enough: more than three-quarters of affected homeowners needed at least two repair attempts or said the problem remained unresolved.
Meanwhile, 61.1% reported recurring issues or were unsure whether the original repair had worked. For homeowners, that can mean repeated disruption as well as mounting bills.

The end of the DLP does not necessarily mean the end of defect problems. Among respondents who experienced waterproofing issues afterwards, 76.3% said these appeared either immediately or within the first year after the period ended.

External walls, bathrooms, balconies and terraces were among the most commonly affected areas, while the warning signs were often familiar ones: mould, damp walls, peeling or bubbling paint, ceiling stains and cracks.

Some of these problems can also spread beyond the original leak. Nearly three in four affected homeowners said waterproofing failures had led to other concerns, including interior damage, mould or hygiene problems, electrical risks and structural damage.

Part of the difficulty is that the place where water appears is not always where it entered. Half of affected homeowners said their biggest challenge was either judging how serious the problem was or identifying its root cause.
Others struggled with choosing the right repair method, knowing whom to trust, and deciding whether the price quoted was reasonable.

That uncertainty may explain why many people wait: 80.4% did not act immediately when they first noticed a problem; instead, they monitored it, waited for it to worsen, or only took action once damage became visible inside the home.
HBA honorary secretary-general Chang Kim Loong said homeowners should document defects early and ensure repairs address the underlying cause rather than simply patching what is visible.
“For homeowners, the end of the DLP should not mean that concerns around the condition of their home simply disappear,” he said.

The survey also found that waterproofing problems affected daily life for 87.6% of those surveyed to some extent, whether through damaged belongings, disruption to routines, stress, health concerns or worries over property value.

Ultimately, a leak is rarely just about the stain you can see. Catching the problem early, keeping records during the DLP, and understanding where the water is actually coming from may help prevent a small defect from becoming a much more expensive one.
bea6ae276ae0bb55: When a child refuses to share a table with another child because one eats pork, we are no longer talking about a minor classroom incident. We are talking about a failure of national education.
Malaysia’s schools are now producing children who see difference as contamination, faith as a barrier, and fellow Malaysians as people to be avoided.
This is not unity. It is segregation being taught early, quietly and dangerously.
A warning from the classroom

Puncak Borneo MP Willie Mongin recently revealed that some primary school pupils had refused to sit beside classmates of another faith. Among the reasons were that a classmate was eating pork or wearing a cross.
Let that sink in.
Children young enough to still be learning multiplication tables are already being taught, directly or indirectly, that another child’s food, religion or symbol makes them unworthy of friendship.
Do not hide behind the excuse that “children repeat what they hear at home”. Of course, families matter.
But schools are where society either corrects prejudice or normalises it. If a child can carry such intolerance into a classroom without being firmly challenged, then the classroom has failed.
Unity cannot remain a slogan
For decades, Malaysia has recited the Rukun Negara, held unity-themed assemblies and printed national slogans on walls, banners and exercise books.
Yet what is the value of a national principle if a child will not sit beside another child because of what that child eats or believes?

The Rukun Negara is not decoration. It is not a mural. It is not a slogan for official events. If it means anything, it must be visible in how children treat one another every day, in classrooms, canteens, playgrounds and school buses.
Our education system has become too comfortable with symbolism. It celebrates diversity on stage but often fails to build genuine relationships across communities in daily school life.
Separate childhoods, divided futures
Malaysia’s national, Chinese and Tamil primary schools reflect our multicultural reality. Preserving mother tongues and cultural identity is legitimate and necessary.
But preserving identity must not mean raising children in social isolation.

When pupils spend their formative years largely among those who look, pray, eat and speak like them, anything different becomes unfamiliar. And unfamiliarity easily induces fear. Fear becomes prejudice. Prejudice breeds rejection.
How can we expect adults to build a united Malaysia if, as children, they were never given real opportunities to know one another?

Joint sports, debates, arts, science projects, community service and shared classrooms must not be occasional photo opportunities. They must be routine, structured and compulsory parts of school life, not pleasing politicians for their occasional visit to school.
Stop pretending the system is fair
We must also stop pretending that education policy is neutral.
For too long, access to opportunities, scholarships, school placements and pathways has been viewed through racial lenses.
Whatever the original intention, the consequence is clear: many young Malaysians grow up believing that their future depends more on their ethnicity than their effort, talent or need.

Helping the disadvantaged is right. But assistance must be transparent, needs-based and accountable. A system that leaves one community feeling privileged and another feeling excluded cannot claim to be building unity.
A child who believes the system does not value them equally will not easily believe the nation values them equally.
Malaysia built on community effort

Our history lessons must stop being exercises in memorising dates and names. They must teach the harder truth: Malaysia was built through negotiation, compromise and cooperation among communities that did not always share the same faith, language or customs.
Tunku Abdul Rahman, Tun Tan Siew Sin and Tun VT Sambanthan came from different communities, yet they worked towards one national objective: independence.
If our founding leaders could sit at the same table and build a nation, why should a child today refuse to sit beside a classmate because of pork or a cross?
No community owns Malaysia. Every community helped build it. Every community has a stake in protecting it.
The education ministry must answer
This is not a problem to be passed to the national unity ministry while the education ministry (MoE) hides behind curriculum documents.
The MoE must answer directly:
Why are children absorbing religious intolerance in schools?
Are teachers trained to identify and confront prejudice early?
Are schools required to create meaningful interaction across communities?
Are incidents of discrimination investigated, recorded and corrected?
Are school leaders held accountable when unity exists only in speeches?
If the ministry cannot enforce the values it preaches, then it is not merely failing pupils. It is failing Malaysia.
Make unity measurable
National unity must become part of every subject, every school and every level of education.
Kindergartens must teach children to play, share and cooperate across backgrounds. Primary and secondary schools must run regular joint programmes with schools of different streams.
History, literature and civics must teach shared nationhood, not narrow narratives. Group work must deliberately bring children out of familiar ethnic and religious circles.

Teachers need training in inclusive classroom practices, religious literacy and conflict resolution. Textbook writers must be held accountable for accuracy, balance and the removal of stereotypes, not mere focus on any one community.
And the ministry must publish measurable indicators: pupils’ sense of belonging, participation in cross-community activities, teacher preparedness, complaints handled and corrective action taken.
Unity must be assessed, not merely announced.
The future is sitting in our classrooms
A child who refuses to share a table today may become an adult who refuses to share a country tomorrow.
This is the harsh truth Malaysia must face: our education system is not merely underperforming academically; it is failing in its duty to mould Malaysians.

We can continue producing students with excellent grades but shallow citizenship. Or we can rebuild schools into places where children learn that faith, food, language and culture must never determine who deserves their friendship.
Malaysia’s future will not be decided only in parliament or boardrooms. It will be decided at classroom tables, where children either learn to see one another as strangers, or as fellow Malaysians.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
62628bc233cbfe52: PETALING JAYA: Potensi nadir bumi (REE) di empat negeri SG4 perlu dibangunkan menerusi kerjasama kerajaan persekutuan dan negeri dengan tumpuan beralih daripada penjualan bahan mentah kepada penguasaan rantaian nilai hiliran.
Pakar industri Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM), Nahrul Khair Alang Md Rashid, berkata pelabur lebih bimbang tentang ketidakpastian dasar dan akses kepada sumber berbanding peraturan ketat.
“Nilai tambahnya terletak pada pemprosesan, pemisahan unsur dan sebagainya iaitu pada proses hiliran.
“Bagaimanapun, sekiranya proses huluan (perlombongan) mengambil masa yang panjang, sudah tentu ia memberi kesan kepada proses hiliran. Kedua-dua proses ini perlu bergerak selari,” katanya kepada FMT.
Beliau berkata, kerjasama pusat-negeri perlu merangkumi persetujuan mengenai dasar, piawaian, keselamatan dan perkongsian manfaat bagi membangunkan industri bernilai tinggi.

Sementara itu, pakar ekonomi alam sekitar Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM), Norlida Hanim Salleh, berkata kekayaan REE perlu dimanfaatkan untuk pembangunan jangka panjang dan kesejahteraan rakyat, bukan sekadar pulangan segera.
Katanya, kebergantungan pada eksport bahan mentah berisiko mewujudkan ‘penjajahan ekonomi baharu’ apabila pemprosesan dan nilai tambah dikuasai pihak luar.

“Sejarah membuktikan kekayaan sumber alam tidak menjamin kemakmuran seimbang. Pembangunan ekonomi berasaskan sumber perlu dinilai menerusi keupayaan membina industri, teknologi dan kemahiran tempatan, bukan sekadar hasil yang dikeluarkan.
“Persoalannya bukan sekadar SG4 kaya dengan REE, tetapi sama ada ia mampu menguasai nilai yang terhasil daripadanya,” katanya.

Norlida berkata, hasil REE perlu diurus secara telus bagi membangunkan modal insan dan industri bernilai tinggi, khususnya ketika Kelantan dan Kedah masing-masing mencatatkan kadar kemiskinan mutlak 11.5% dan 8.5%.
SG4 merangkumi Kedah, Terengganu, Perlis dan Kelantan yang diterajui Perikatan Nasional (PN), dengan tiga daripadanya dikuasai PAS.
Isnin lalu, bekas perdana menteri Dr Mahathir Mohamad menyifatkan gabungan itu sebagai ‘gergasi tidur’ yang berpotensi menggandakan ekonomi negara.
Penasihat SG4 itu berkata, negeri terbabit perlu mengelakkan penjualan bahan mentah secara langsung dan mengutamakan strategi tambah nilai demi manfaat mampan kepada rakyat.
7d85d152caf321b1: LOS ANGELES: Dolores Huerta, the US labour leader and civil rights icon whose union work changed the lives of migrant workers, has died, her family said Wednesday. She was 96.

For nearly four decades Huerta was vice-president of the United Farm Workers, the union she founded with Cesar Chavez, organising strikes and walkouts that won improvements in working conditions for the millions of men and women who labour in US fields.
"We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96," said a family statement.
"We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning, and we will be following up on plans to recognize and celebrate her incredible life and legacy."
Erik Olvera, a spokesman for her family, told AFP Wednesday that Huerta died of cancer in the morning surrounded by loved ones.
Born in New Mexico and raised in California, Huerta took the reins of the US farmworker movement in the 1960s with Chavez.
At the time, she was raising seven children -- she later had more -- while going through a divorce.
While Huerta was the organising force behind the union, Chavez was its charismatic leader and the public face who became an icon to generations on the left, even after his death in 1993.
But that fame and the seemingly tight relationship between him and Huerta hid a dark secret that came to light this year, when Huerta said she was one of a number of women Chavez had raped.
In her case, the attacks resulted in two pregnancies.

"The first time... I didn't feel I could say no because he was someone that I admired, my boss and the leader of the movement I had already devoted years of my life to," she said in a statement to the New York Times, which broke the story.
"The second time I was forced, against my will, and in an environment where I felt trapped."

Huerta remained a galvanising figure in left-wing politics well into her 90s, helping to organise a fightback among migrant labourers targeted by President Donald Trump's immigration swoops that saw farmworkers snatched from the fields by masked federal agents.

"People are reaching out because they want to do something," she told AFP during a July 2025 interview at the headquarters of her Dolores Huerta Foundation in Bakersfield, an agricultural nexus in California's Central Valley.
"We've got to be a lot more active, because what's happening right now is so huge. I liken it to what was happening in Germany before Hitler took power," she said.
'The best of us'
Huerta rubbed shoulders with some of America's most influential people over decades in the public eye.
In 1968, she stood on a podium alongside Democratic presidential hopeful Robert F. Kennedy, brother of assassinated former president John F. Kennedy, just minutes before he was shot dead.
Former president Barack Obama -- whose "Yes, we can" slogan he acknowledged he adopted from Huerta's "Si se puede" -- awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom when he was in the White House.
News of Huerta's death prompted Obama to once again emphasize that she coined the slogan, which he noted "I too often get credit for."
"As usual, Dolores got there first."
"Michelle and I are thinking of Dolores's family, the people whose lives she changed, and everyone who drew inspiration from her example," the former president said in a statement on social media.
Obama was among a chorus of figures across the worlds of politics and advocacy who paid tribute to Huerta.
Governor Gavin Newsom ordered flags flown at half-staff in her honor, saying "Dolores represented the best of us" in her work that "changed the course of history against all odds."
Former president Bill Clinton praised her as a "dear friend" and "stalwart champion of working Americans."
"To see her in action was to witness a living legend who never stopped pushing for progress," Clinton said in a statement, "even as those efforts sometimes brought her grave consequences."
And California Representative Nancy Pelosi lauded Huerta's "courage and determination," saying the activist "inspired generations of Americans to believe in the power of collective action."

93533a177499b9fe: PARIS: European aircraft manufacturer Airbus said Wednesday its third quarter revenues dipped as it finished fewer planes, but insisted it would still deliver a record number this year.

Airbus kept to its target of delivering a record 870 commercial aircraft this year, beating the 863 it handed over to airlines in 2019 before the Covid pandemic upended the industry.
"Against a complex geopolitical and operating environment, we are focused on delivery while maintaining a steadfast focus on quality," chief executive Guillaume Faury said in a statement.
"Our plan is clear, and our teams are onboard to meet our objectives," he added.
Aircraft deliveries are important for Airbus and its main competitor Boeing as they get paid the majority of the agreed price when planes are hand over.

3f40214d76a7be3b: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 29 — No startup has ever grown so fast. In five years, Anthropic has become an AI giant valued at US$1 trillion (RM4.08 trillion), and it is now aiming for a record-breaking stock market debut.
But it faces three threats: rivals that are catching up, prices that are collapsing, and bills that keep climbing.
Anthropic spells out the risks in its Wall Street prospectus, published Monday.
The first is commoditisation: “the degree of differentiation among advanced AI models may narrow,” the company warns.

The San Francisco-based firm also says “substantially all of our revenue” comes from its AI tools. Unlike Google or Meta, it has no advertising empire to fall back on if business takes a hit, and no cloud business like Microsoft’s or SpaceX’s.
Investors have already grown nervous. In mid-August, shareholders were floating a valuation of US$2 trillion.
But quarter-on-quarter growth slowed from 145 per cent in the second quarter to 45 per cent in the third, cooling expectations to around US$1.5 trillion.
Cheap and open
So-called open AI models, which anyone can download and modify, are close behind closed models such as Claude or ChatGPT, which are available only through their owners’ paid services.
The performance of open models trails by only about four months on average, according to research institute Epoch AI.
They include Kimi K3.1 Pro from Chinese company Moonshot, which costs half as much as Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic’s current flagship.
And among paid models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google, none has stayed on top for long.
Anthropic also acknowledges it is holding itself back: its safety measures “could slow our capability gains relative to competitors that do not adopt similar constraints.”
Still, the company says each new version of Claude has boosted sales. More than 80 per cent of its revenue last quarter came from models less than six months old.
Prices collapsing

When products look alike, prices fall. According to Morningstar, the price of having AI process the same amount of text, at the same level of performance, has dropped 97 per cent, from US$17 at the end of 2024 to 50 cents today.
Anthropic itself cut the price of Claude Opus by 20 per cent in September, and OpenAI cut the price of one of its flagship models by a factor of five in July.
The effect is already visible at Vercel, a developer platform that routes requests across AI models.
In August, more than half of the text it handled was processed by open models, up from 13 per cent in April.
Even so, Anthropic still captured nearly two-thirds of spending on the platform.
Even a 90 per cent price cut would not shrink total spending on AI as long as usage keeps growing at its current pace, said Malik Ahmed Khan, a senior equity analyst at Morningstar.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Traffic transits past Anthropic’s headquarters in San Francisco, California October 27, 2026. — Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images/AFP pic
‘Triple whammy’
Anthropic’s costs, by contrast, are largely locked in. To stay ahead, each new Claude model has to be bigger than the last, trained on more data using more computing power.
Since late 2025, the company has committed to paying at least US$417 billion to rent chips and servers.
That is nearly 13 years of sales at its first-half 2026 pace, and the total could nearly double if cancellable or planned contracts are included.
These commitments are due no matter the state of its business, Anthropic warns.
The bet involves the entire industry: Google and Amazon are at once Anthropic’s shareholders, its suppliers and its resellers.

If AI turns out to be less profitable than expected, the International Monetary Fund fears a “triple whammy” from these intertwined investments: falling stock prices, debts that are harder to repay, and promised revenue that never materialises.
The independent research firm New Constructs called the listing “an unprecedented test of investor gullibility.”
To pay these bills, Anthropic is counting on money from the stock market, which is not unlimited.
SpaceX, Elon Musk’s rocket and AI company, raised record sums there in June, while Google and Meta, which are pouring fortunes into data centres, are also seeking fresh capital.
OpenAI, whose chief Sam Altman called a listing “ill-advised” this year, has chosen to wait until 2027, giving it time to see how Wall Street treats its big rival. — AFP

ef016c6396d52f41: SAN FRANCISCO: Microsoft shares popped more than 5% Wednesday afternoon after it reported better than expected revenue and profit, fuelled by its Azure cloud computing division which grew by 48% in the September quarter.
"We are delivering greater capability, choice, control, and cost efficiency for customers across our entire stack," Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said in a statement.

Analysts had expected around US$90.6 billion in revenue and US$35.1 billion in profit, according to FactSet.

The quarterly earnings report comes just days after Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as the tech giant spends heavily on artificial intelligence investments.
It's the second voluntary buyout offer that Microsoft has offered employees this year, after giving seven percent of its US workforce the option to retire early in April.

Microsoft will hold a call with analysts on Wednesday afternoon to discuss its quarterly results.
AI spending
One of the big questions looming over tech earnings is whether the industry's heavy AI spending is paying off.
Analysts are expecting US$51 billion in overall spending by Microsoft from July to September, according to FactSet.
Microsoft nearly doubled its spending on "property and equipment" to US$39 billion compared to the same period last year, according to a press release.
It competes with Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google parent Alphabet for cloud computing services customers.

Microsoft is number two globally, followed by Google.

c65342f42e85a766: WASHINGTON: Shares in Google parent Alphabet fell more than 10% in after-hours trading Wednesday as the company reported lower-than-expected profit and a slowdown in its advertising business while it maintained big spending on AI.
Net profit slid 25% from a year earlier to US$26.2 billion in the July-to-September period, or US$2.12 per share, well short of expectations by analysts surveyed by FactSet.
Alphabet booked an US$8.7 billion loss on its equity investments, which it attributed to its stake in SpaceX, the Elon Musk-led company where shares have struggled since going public in June.
Revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion, slightly below the roughly US$128 billion analysts had forecast.

Advertising revenue grew 11% to US$82.0 billion, short of expectations. Revenue from Google's search business, still the company's largest source of income, rose 12% to US$63.4 billion, slowing from 17% growth in the previous quarter.

YouTube, now the most-watched content provider on American TV screens, saw advertising revenue grow 9% to US$11.2 billion, down from 13% growth in the previous quarter. YouTube Music and Premium passed 150 million subscribers worldwide, including trials.
Google Cloud, which rents computing power and AI tools to businesses, saw revenue jump 103% to US$30.7 billion, ahead of analyst expectations.
The company said sales of its in-house AI chips, known as TPUs, contributed significantly to that growth. Operating income for the unit tripled to US$11.1 billion.
Google is also selling its TPU chips to outside companies, in a growing challenge to market leader Nvidia. OpenAI plans to buy some of the chips, according to media reports this week.
Alphabet's "Other Bets" division, which includes robotaxi company Waymo, posted revenue of US$372 million and an operating loss of US$2.0 billion.
Waymo now provides more than 500,000 paid rides per week across 15 US metropolitan areas and aims to reach one million weekly rides by the end of the year.
'Long-range planning'
Alphabet spent US$51.4 billion on capital expenditures during the quarter, mostly on data centres and AI chips, more than double the US$24 billion a year earlier.
Its latest forecast for capex spending is between US$195 billion to US$205 billion in spending for 2026.
The company said it would continue to increase capex spending significantly in 2027.
"I would broadly think of all of this as a long-range planning process, not a short-term allocation exercise," Google CEO Sundar Pichai told analysts of the company's investment splurge.
The company's spending, which included a fine paid to the European Union, outstripped the cash generated by Alphabet's businesses for a second straight quarter, leaving a US$9.1 billion gap.
During the quarter Alphabet raised US$28.7 billion by selling bonds and US$12.4 billion by issuing new shares to help pay for its AI ambitions.
Google has stepped up the pace of its AI releases since a delay to a flagship model in July raised questions about whether it was falling behind rivals OpenAI and Anthropic.
It launched Gemini 4 at the end of September and later released a version focused on cybersecurity.
The Gemini app has reached one billion users. Google's AI models now process nearly 32 billion tokens, or units of text, per minute, more than four times the level of a year ago, the company said.
Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, is also one of Google's largest cloud customers. It has committed to using up to one million Google AI chips.
In September, a US judge declined to order Google to sell off parts of its advertising technology business, imposing restrictions on how it operates instead.

c8560039871f83cb: NEW YORK: US stock indexes advanced on Wednesday after the US Federal Reserve left its key policy rate unchanged, as widely expected, leaving investors betting on a rate hike at its next monetary policy meeting in December.

f162e85f08293df4: WASHINGTON: The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday held interest rates steady, even as its chairman Kevin Warsh said inflation remained "too high" but insisted that politics played no part in the central bank's decision not to continue raising rates days before crucial midterm elections.

The 12-member Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 to 4.00 percent, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation, after having hiked for the first time in three years at its previous meeting in September.
Two members of the committee, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented, calling instead for an immediate quarter-point rate hike.
"Energy and related prices have moved higher again in recent weeks, and our job is to ensure that relative price changes in some sectors do not broaden out across the economy," Warsh told reporters.
Still, he said the FOMC needed more information in the coming weeks to "determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the two-percent goal."
The committee is scheduled to meet again in early December.
'Politics played no role'
The central bank has missed its inflation target for more than five years, with households and businesses battered by sustained price increases.
US President Donald Trump's war on Iran, launched in late February, has sent energy prices skyrocketing and fueled domestic inflation, alongside his wide-ranging tariff policies.
Prices have also been driven by an investment boom in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and the build-out of huge data centers to support it.
The decision comes six days ahead of the Nov 3 midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party is seeking to wrest control of both houses of Congress from Trump's Republicans.

Trump's handling of the economy has been a key issue throughout the campaign, with working-class households across the country struggling to make ends meet despite largely stable overall economic growth.
US consumer inflation came in hotter than expected in September, clocking in at 3.7%, edging back towards a three-year high established in May.
"Politics played no role in the decision," said Warsh, who has insisted that he supports the Fed's independence despite repeated attacks on the institution by Trump since he took office.
Speaking to broadcaster CNBC after the Fed's meeting, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he and Trump had "great confidence" in Warsh.

"I have great confidence in Chair Warsh to steer the Fed between the right combination of growth and inflation because what you don't want to do is cause enough of a growth slowdown that energy consumption would drop," he said.
'Strong' economic growth
On Wednesday, the Fed said economic activity in the US was expanding at a "strong" pace, upgrading its language from the FOMC meeting six weeks prior.
At his press conference, Warsh spoke to that theme, and questioned whether the AI-led investment boom was fuelling inflation.
"Is the economy running too hot? Is the economy running too strong? That isn't the judgment of most of my colleagues," he said.
In a significant move, Warsh also announced that the Fed would be reducing the number of times it sets interest rates in the next two years.
It will continue to meet eight times a year in 2027 and 2028, but will only set interest rates seven times next year and six times the year after that.
"Getting policy right involves assessing near-term developments at timely, regular, and information-rich intervals," said Warsh.
"But it's equally important we reserve time and space as an intellectually diverse group for strategic deliberations, for thinking anew about big questions, looking out over longer time horizons."
'Don't understand the logic'

Wendy Edelberg, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, told AFP before the meeting that a decision to hold after raising rates in September was potentially contradictory, given the labor market -- the Fed's other mandate -- has been largely stable.
"In terms of the economics of it, I don't totally understand the logic," she said.
"If there was a reason to raise interest rates at the last meeting, I think that there's just as compelling of an economic reason to raise interest rates at this meeting."
The Fed has a dual mandate to maintain maximum employment while keeping inflation to its long-term target.

It achieves this goal largely using one tool: the economy's key interest rate. Raising rates tends to cool inflation but can also dampen economic activity; lowering them can spur economic activity but also fuel inflation.
The US unemployment rate has been largely stable around 4.2% over the last year, with job growth mostly in positive territory -- albeit driven by a few sectors.
Other advanced economies have also been grappling with high inflation, and on Wednesday Canada's central bank raised its key rate to 2.5%, its first hike since July 2023.
